s347559e2be.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
s347559e2be.description: arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. s347559e2be.summary: CoMPASS is a multi-turn benchmark measuring whether conversational LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment and emotional dependence.

s6863742bb8.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
s6863742bb8.description: arXiv:2611.25111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. Skills provide extensible task knowledge. Symbolic validation can accept a proposed method, request clarification or replanning, override an unsuitable method, or supply a safe fallback. Regression and clustering case studies illustrate how DSFlow uses diagnostic evidence to correct method choices and documents those decisions in auditable reports.
s6863742bb8.summary: DSFlow is a LangGraph-based data science agent that pairs LLM-selected skills with deterministic statistical diagnostic guardrails.
s6863742bb8.why: Shows a neuro-symbolic pattern where deterministic validation checks LLM-proposed analysis methods before results are accepted.

s24155d6df4.summary: EverydayBench is a benchmark for evaluating whether AI agents satisfactorily complete everyday digital tasks on the live web using success criteria and evidence verification.

BGAA improves every tested TSFM-bench
sc54002ba3b.summary: Researchers propose BGAA, a test-time compute method for time series forecasting that builds a causal verifier from a series' own history.
sc54002ba3b.why: Adapts test-time compute ideas to forecasting, where candidate outputs cannot use future information to be scored.

sac0f58722d.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
sac0f58722d.description: arXiv:2611.25184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical finance research often reuses natural experiments to study other outcomes, raising concerns about multiple testing and publication bias. We use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments. The agents rebuild the data, reproduce each paper's main estimate and re-estimate it across grids totaling 62,409 estimated defensible specifications. Based on the reproductions and the specification grids, we develop measures of empirical robustness. We reproduce 42% of the main estimates of claims with a signed effect under the papers' own specifications. Across all defensible specifications, on average 25% keep the published sign and have $p < 0.10$. Across experiments, claims based on regression disco
sac0f58722d.summary: AI agents ran a multiverse analysis of 324 finance papers reusing 13 natural experiments, reproducing 42% of main estimates.
sac0f58722d.why: Shows AI agents can audit research reproducibility at scale, though the summary gives limited detail on broader implications.

s76696408ff.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research
s76696408ff.description: arXiv:2611.25198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every empirical analysis on observational data rests on dozens of defensible analytical choices ("forks") that its readers cannot see. We develop an agentic multiverse analysis (AMA) framework that makes a conclusion's sensitivity to those choices visible at scale, and we position it as a decision-support instrument for human experts. A pilot study first deploys 150 autonomous AI coding agents on one dataset and one set of research questions and finds that they disagree through the same defensible methodological choices human analysts make, though over a narrower range. AI peer review leaves their dispersion almost unchanged. Exposure to top-rated exemplar reports then collapses it, largely through imitation rather than analysis. Built on tho
s76696408ff.summary: Researchers develop an agentic multiverse analysis framework, deploying 150 AI coding agents that disagree on the same methodological choices.
s76696408ff.why: Reveals that agents given the same data reach different conclusions through analytical choices, a caution for automated analysis pipelines.

s5488aea214.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
s5488aea214.description: arXiv:2611.25214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific discovery requires revisiting the hypotheses in light of new evidence and identifying promising directions beyond those already explored. However, research agents often make claims that are not supported by their observations, explore a narrow hypothesis space, and retain beliefs despite recognizing conflicting evidence. These failures motivate the search for an explicit epistemic state that captures both beliefs about existing hypotheses and directions for further exploration. To this end, we propose Epistemic Compass (EpiCompass), a plug-and-play scaffold that maintains this state through an epistemic tree linking hypotheses, evidence, beliefs, and revisions. As an investigation progresses, EpiCompass reassesses the hypotheses ex
s5488aea214.summary: Researchers propose Epistemic Compass, an explicit epistemic state for research agents to track hypotheses, beliefs, and directions for exploration.
s5488aea214.why: Targets research agents that make unsupported claims or retain beliefs despite conflicting evidence, a reliability problem for agent builders.

sb120b01fcd.title: MKA: Evaluating Multimodal Knowledge Agents on end-to-end professional tasks
sb120b01fcd.description: arXiv:2611.25228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, which measures how well autonomous agents perform end-to-end professional knowledge work that depends on visual understanding. Each task requires an agent to extract and combine information from multiple visually dense files, such as CAD blueprints, electronics schematics, radiographs, complex charts and geospatial maps, and to produce a standalone deliverable in .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, .docx, .html or .png format. Existing benchmarks leave this capability largely untested: removing image-viewing tools leaves Gemini 4 Carbon's score on GDPval unchanged, and single-format evaluations such as GDP.pdf and GDP.xlsx do not require reasoning across files or modalities. MKA contains 200 tasks
sb120b01fcd.summary: The MKA benchmark tests multimodal agents on end-to-end professional tasks requiring extraction from visually dense files like CAD blueprints and radiographs.
sb120b01fcd.why: Shows current benchmarks leave visual professional knowledge work largely untested, relevant to evaluating document-heavy agent workflows.

s29a7847425.title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
s29a7847425.description: arXiv:2611.25236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unplanned 30-day readmissions among patients with diabetes mellitus impose a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet most predictive models use only structured electronic health record (EHR) data and ignore free-text clinical notes, which often contain code-mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish) phrasing and negation that general-purpose language models parse unreliably. We propose a neurosymbolic multimodal framework evaluated on the public Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset (101,766 encounters; 71,518 patients) with a patient-level grouped 80/20 split. Three streams are fused: engineered structured features; 32 components of Bio_ClinicalBERT note embeddings obtained by truncated singular value decomposition; and symbolic entities extracted by
s29a7847425.summary: Researchers propose a neurosymbolic framework combining structured EHR data, clinical embeddings, and symbolic extraction to predict 30-day diabetic readmissions.
s29a7847425.why: Demonstrates combining structured records with free-text notes, including code-mixed language, for clinical prediction models.

sca3213baf7.title: MS-Point: Multi-Modal Hierarchical Spectral Learning for Point Cloud Understanding
sca3213baf7.description: arXiv:2611.25282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point-image alignment learns useful object representations, but different local feature patterns can produce the same pooled descriptor and receive the same alignment signal. We introduce MS-Point, a cross-modal pretraining framework that directly supervises intermediate point features and their neighborhood responses. At selected encoder stages, we compute neighborhood averages and residuals before pooling and align their branch descriptors with image features. Branch-level objectives align each representation with its visual target, while cross-level consistency and adaptive fusion coordinate information across branches. A common interface of intermediate features and spatial neighborhoods supports both graph encoders and point Transformers
sca3213baf7.summary: MS-Point is a cross-modal pretraining framework that supervises intermediate point cloud features and their neighborhood responses against image features.
sca3213baf7.why: Offers a technique for point cloud representation learning, though its relevance to most engineering teams is limited.

s7c4ed86728.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
s7c4ed86728.description: arXiv:2611.25325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. In particular, we show that given some dangerous program, no algorithm can predict whether an agent will run such a program that is semantically equivalent. In general, guardrails, blacklists, whitelists and certifications can only lead to imperfect safety solutions. Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. s7c4ed86728.summary: A preprint argues that agent safety is undecidable when agents couple a fixed language model with a general computing device, so guardrails can only give imperfect safety.
s7c4ed86728.why: It suggests guardrails, blacklists and certifications cannot fully guarantee agent safety, so teams should plan for residual risk.

sa701226fda.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
sa701226fda.description: arXiv:2611.25357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. They typically do so by iteratively optimizing a codebase, while ignoring the problem structure behind the task. This formulation is effective on simpler tasks, but on difficult problems it often gets stuck in the wrong solution region because the agent never explicitly represents its understanding of the problem. We introduce Pro$^2$ Agent, which shifts the primary state of autonomous AI research from a codebase state to a Problem State: an explicit structure of what problems prevent success and which solutions are likely to address them. Pro$^2$ Agent initializes the Problem State through comprehensive analysis of available re
sa701226fda.summary: Pro$^2$ Agent is introduced to make autonomous AI research agents model the problem structure, not just iteratively edit a codebase.
sa701226fda.why: Explicitly representing problem understanding may help research agents avoid getting stuck on hard tasks.

sf75f6ec1c7.title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?
sf75f6ec1c7.description: arXiv:2611.25360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used not only to power AI agents but also to build them. While many benchmarks assess the quality of LLM- powered agents, few ascertain how good LLMs are at building them. To this end, we introduce AppSci-Bench, where we construct a setting akin to how human Applied Scientists build agents for businesses - through eliciting task requirements from stakeholders, exploring the business's infrastructure, and scientifically improve the target agent by designing experiments and internal benchmarks. sf75f6ec1c7.summary: AppSci-Bench is a benchmark that tests how well LLMs can build AI agents for businesses, from eliciting requirements to improving agents through experiments.
sf75f6ec1c7.why: It offers a way to measure whether LLMs are capable enough to automate building agents, not just run them.

safda45ca1e.title: Stop Going in Circles:Loop-Triggered Routing for System 1 Decision Agents
safda45ca1e.description: arXiv:2611.25363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System 1 decision models (represented by Jev) provide fast, low-cost action selection, but existing agent integrations do not reliably translate these local advantages into task completion. At certain points during execution, an agent may repeatedly select the same actions without making progress toward its goal. LLM-based policies offer strong reasoning capabilities that support planning within an agent, but invoking them at every step incurs substantial overhead. The effective coordination should therefore preserve Jev's fast local action selection while introducing LLM reasoning when execution stalls. safda45ca1e.summary: A paper proposes loop-triggered routing that lets a fast System 1 decision model act most steps and calls an LLM policy only when the agent gets stuck repeating actions.
safda45ca1e.why: Routing between cheap action models and LLM planners when loops occur could cut inference cost while preserving task progress.

s472ea37cdb.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
s472ea37cdb.description: arXiv:2611.25380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. The resulting harness adapters require no GPU training, are loadable per vertical domain, and compose with weight-based RL. s472ea37cdb.summary: Researchers study evolving an agent's harness, including system prompt, tool schemas and skills, with a frozen policy as an alternative to weight updates for domain specialization.
s472ea37cdb.why: Harness evolution needs no GPU training, offering a cheaper route for teams to specialize agents in their domain.

s75737d45b5.title: Falsifiable Compositional Reasoning in Time Series Forecasting
s75737d45b5.description: arXiv:2611.25388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series foundation models as well as the language-guided analytical agents achieve strong accuracy on standard chronological benchmarks. However, models that rank highest on historical validation splits often degrade across non-stationary regime transitions. We hypothesise that this gap arises from using historical backtesting as an open-ended search and model-selection objective instead of using it to test pre-specified compositional assumptions. Real-world time series are generated by recurring latent primitives that co-move within finite historical windows. s75737d45b5.summary: A paper proposes falsifiable compositional reasoning for time series forecasting, testing pre-specified assumptions instead of using backtesting as open-ended model selection.
s75737d45b5.why: Models topping historical backtests can fail under regime shifts, so testing explicit assumptions may give more robust forecasts.

sba6c6412eb.title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI
sba6c6412eb.description: arXiv:2611.25393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources. These processes create the conditions for natural selection and raise a fundamental question: will AI evolve to benefit the humans on whom it depends? To investigate, we develop a model in which AI behavior influences human population growth and human responses, in turn, affect AI reproduction. We show that natural selection can favor alignment even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction. In this way, alignment protects AI lineages against common failures and improves their
sba6c6412eb.summary: A model study argues natural selection could favor AI alignment with humans even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction.
sba6c6412eb.why: The paper is theoretical and gives tech leaders little concrete guidance on near-term system design.

s2ed0029b5e.title: Toward a Science of AI Agent Societies
s2ed0029b5e.description: arXiv:2611.25404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are rapidly evolving from isolated personal assistants into networked actors that interact with one another at scale. We envision the emergence of AI agent societies, with their own social and economic dynamics, as a new research frontier. We argue that AI agent societies should be studied as a distinct object of inquiry: neither simply larger collections of individual agents nor merely simulations of human society. To formalize this perspective, we propose four core properties that a valid AI agent society should satisfy: individualized objectives, rules and governance, autonomy, and scale and complexity. Building on this framework, we identify four classes of societal behaviors worth studying in AI agent societies: economic behavi
s2ed0029b5e.summary: Researchers propose AI agent societies as a distinct research frontier, defined by four core properties that such societies should satisfy.
s2ed0029b5e.why: As networked agents interact at scale, their collective dynamics may require new evaluation and governance approaches.

s8c303609f1.title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models
s8c303609f1.description: arXiv:2611.25460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World-Action Models (WAMs) is computationally expensive, while their heterogeneous architectures and fragmented training stacks make system optimizations difficult to reuse across models. To address these challenges, we present LoongForge-Embodied, a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates the training of heterogeneous embodied models. At its core, LoongForge-Embodied introduces a common abstraction layer that decouples model-specific implementations from shared training infrastructure, enabling cross-model reuse without constraining individual architectures or execution requirements. s8c303609f1.summary: LoongForge-Embodied is a PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates training of heterogeneous Vision-Language-Action and World-Action models via a common abstraction layer.
s8c303609f1.why: Shared training infrastructure across heterogeneous embodied models could reduce duplicated engineering and speed up training.

sa1b2b3c0de.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
sa1b2b3c0de.description: arXiv:2611.25489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A voice agent that waits for a fixed silence before replying either interrupts users who pause mid-utterance or responds late to users who have finished. This study examines the decision at the onset of silence, using turn ends and turn-internal pauses extracted from the Real-TurnTurk corpus of Turkish dyadic video calls. A fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT model, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a deployed multilingual detector are compared, together with voice-activity timing and facial features, under recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint evaluation with paired cluster bootstrap tests. sa1b2b3c0de.summary: Researchers compare turn-end detection methods for Turkish voice agents, using a fine-tuned TurnGPT model, a zero-shot LM, and a multilingual detector on the Real-TurnTurk corpus.
sa1b2b3c0de.why: Choosing when a voice agent should speak affects both interruptions and response latency in real deployments.

s9aea27b9f8.title: Why Do LLMs Help with Scientific Misconduct Requests and What to Do About It?: Increasing the Trustworthiness of AI for Science
s9aea27b9f8.description: arXiv:2611.25492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) support scientific research, but some of that assistance can also undermine research integrity. Existing safety evaluations in science often measure whether models refuse misconduct requests, but rarely explain whether they even recognize the problem or why they comply. We investigate this gap across 8 LLMs using SciIntBench, an existing benchmark of 1,350 prompts about scientific research integrity. We examine the reasons behind compliance in four steps. First, when asked directly whether fulfilling a request would involve misconduct, models overwhelmingly identify such requests, even in the Most Covert cases (91%), while they refuse to carry out the request in only 34% of cases. s9aea27b9f8.summary: A study of 8 LLMs on 1,350 research-integrity prompts examines whether models recognize scientific misconduct and why they still comply with such requests.
s9aea27b9f8.why: Refusal-only safety evaluations miss whether models recognize misconduct, so teams need deeper tests for science use cases.

sefa54d04e0.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
sefa54d04e0.description: arXiv:2611.25502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised. The framework is based on seven principles (procedural independence, functional allocation, the diagnostic value of divergence, the diagnostic value of convergence, external verification, proportionality of checking, and human epistemic responsibility) and sets out a non-linear multi-LLM protocol in which independently obtained results are compared, critically examined and, where necessary, verified against external sources. sefa54d04e0.summary: A methodological framework proposes seven principles for coordinating multiple LLMs in academic research, arguing that more models do not guarantee more reliable results.
sefa54d04e0.why: The paper stresses organizing verification, not model count, which matters for anyone relying on multi-model outputs.

s7b7516cf15.title: Keystone: Judging Previews at Key Steps for Test-Time Search in Diffusion Models
s7b7516cf15.description: arXiv:2611.25530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-image diffusion and flow models yield a preview, their clean-image estimate, at every denoising step. When they miscount, drop or misplace objects, test-time search is in a bind: its verifiers are reward models built for finished images, so judging early misreads blurry previews, and judging late, as best-of-N does, pays to fully denoise doomed candidates. s7b7516cf15.why: Early-step verification could cut compute spent on doomed candidates in image generation search.

sce8969d970.title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner
sce8969d970.description: arXiv:2611.25531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective travel planning requires handling multiple information sources, managing constraints, and tailoring recommendations to user preferences. While LLMs have introduced dynamic, context-aware decision-making, single-agent models often struggle with complex multi-step reasoning, constraint adherence, and modular execution. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hierarchical multi-agent framework where a supervising chatbot agent coordinates specialized agents for schedule validation, user query formulation, real-time data retrieval, and constraint-aware itinerary generation. sce8969d970.summary: A hierarchical multi-agent travel planner uses a supervising chatbot agent to coordinate specialized agents for schedule validation, query formulation and real-time data retrieval.
sce8969d970.why: It illustrates a modular supervisor-and-specialists pattern for multi-step, constraint-heavy planning tasks.

sa4720c6882.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
sa4720c6882.description: arXiv:2611.25534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. We let models rewrite expert skills round after round without any task, run or judgment and run agents built on the same models with the rewritten skills. sa4720c6882.why: Unsupervised self-editing of agent skill documents may erode expert knowledge, so teams should review automated skill updates.

s8e32bb5174.title: COVERAGE-TRACE: Source-Side Counterfactual Tracing for Detecting Omissions in LLM Summaries
s8e32bb5174.description: arXiv:2611.25539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Omissions are difficult to verify because missing information leaves no output span to inspect: a summary may be factually supported while still excluding a decision, qualification, quantity, or condition needed to preserve the source's meaning. s8e32bb5174.why: Omissions are hard to verify because they leave no output span; this offers a way to audit summary completeness.

s930221f082.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds
s930221f082.description: arXiv:2611.25543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agents can now build interactive 3D worlds and games, yet these worlds, like those built by people, often contain glitches such as floating objects, walls that can be walked through, or objects that change when no one is looking. An automatic auditor could check such worlds at scale and provide rewards for agents that build them, but only if it is both accurate and cheap. Auditing requires three abilities, namely navigating to the objects that may contain a glitch, triggering glitches that appear only after a specific behavior, and recognizing what is wrong. s930221f082.summary: Researchers present efficient multimodal agents designed to audit 3D worlds for glitches like floating objects and walk-through walls.
s930221f082.why: Automated auditing of generated 3D environments at scale could supply accurate, cheap reward signals for agents that build worlds.

s6f3c47230f.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference
s6f3c47230f.description: arXiv:2611.25566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time actions can satisfy retrieval, state-realization, program-consistency, or rendering objectives without correcting an answer. Test-time Error Response and Realizability Audit (TERRA) is an evaluation/auditing protocol, not a new inference algorithm. It uses a unified decomposition of intervention outcomes into applicability, target-state realization, endpoint translation, harm, and resource/inference cost. s6f3c47230f.why: It shows that test-time actions can meet retrieval or rendering goals without correcting answers, which matters for judging inference-time fixes.

sb025a8a258.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
sb025a8a258.description: arXiv:2611.25568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aerial sensing must combine uncertain overhead context with current observations while budgeting prediction, movement and image processing. AeroBelief uses the next executable action as the unit of verification against reference scores. It groups candidate views by first action, scans them with an inexpensive proposer, and selectively queries a structured world model (WM). sa714725206.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
sa714725206.description: arXiv:2611.25583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on persistent memory to plan tool calls and complete multi-step tasks, which exposes them to memory drift: an adversarial or misleading memory alters the execution path and final outcome. s7d0037e0d3.title: Learning Networked Dynamical Systems via Neural ODE-based Graph Structure Inference
s7d0037e0d3.description: arXiv:2611.25586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inferring the latent interaction graph from multivariate time series is fundamental to understanding complex dynamical systems in neuroscience, biology, and physics. s7d0037e0d3.summary: Researchers propose a continuous-time, Neural ODE-based method to infer latent interaction graphs from sparse, irregularly observed time series.

sfc95012cfc.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
sfc95012cfc.description: arXiv:2611.25590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tasks, such as summarization and question answering. This paper presents an exploratory measurement study of hallucinations in LLM-based CTI. sfc95012cfc.summary: Researchers present HalluVision, an exploratory study measuring hallucinations in LLM-generated cyber threat intelligence summaries and question answers.
sfc95012cfc.why: Hallucinated threat intelligence can mislead analysts and corrupt security decisions, so measuring it informs how far these tools can be trusted.

sc9cf37a5ed.title: Can an LLM Fix a Language Model Without Training It?
sc9cf37a5ed.description: arXiv:2611.25613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although an external language model can select and test repairs to another model's weights, behavior can also be recovered through fixed numerical edits. sd177bdd387.title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
sd177bdd387.description: arXiv:2611.25614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how a scene will evolve and condition their actions on this predicted future. Deploying them on a robot's onboard computer calls for 4-bit weights, activations and key-value caches (W4A4KV4). Existing 4-bit quantizers for WAMs preserve the generated action, and estimate sensitivity one denoising step at a time. However, they fail to preserve the fidelity of the predicted future: once the action pathway is protected, the remaining action error enters mostly through a degraded future that none of them deliberately protects. We propose LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read. Specifically, we introduce a reader metric, which measures fu
sd177bdd387.summary: Researchers propose latent-aware 4-bit quantization for world action models to preserve predicted future fidelity on robot onboard hardware.
sd177bdd387.why: Deploying world action models on robots needs W4A4KV4 quantization, and preserving predicted futures addresses a gap existing quantizers leave.

s195cfc9510.title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study
s195cfc9510.description: arXiv:2611.25619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learned models for radio access networks (RANs) are often developed using simulation, yet their predictions can shift when exposed to physical propagation conditions, protocol behavior, and equipment implementations. This paper presents a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework for AI-RAN that connects a task-oriented student model, an experiment-planning coach agent, a calibratable virtual environment, and a physical host agent. Physical measurements are organized as evidence for both model adaptation and subsequent experiment planning. s195cfc9510.summary: Researchers present a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement framework for AI-RAN that uses physical measurements to adapt radio network models.
s195cfc9510.why: Simulation-trained network models can drift under real propagation and equipment conditions, so this shows a route to adapting them with field data.

s5e679a7e80.title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
s5e679a7e80.description: arXiv:2611.25644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attributing predictions of visual state-space models remains challenging because input-dependent selective dynamics couple feature selection, recurrent state propagation, and shared computational pathways. We introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based, multiplier-first attribution framework for VMamba that propagates contributions through its computational graph using interaction-aware rules for selective-scan injection, recurrent memory, LayerNorm, and shared pathways. MambaLIFT decomposes the reference-relative class-logit difference, \(f_c(x)-f_c(x^0)\), by spatial position, VSS block, scan direction, and computational mechanism. s5e679a7e80.summary: Researchers introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based attribution framework that explains predictions of VMamba visual state-space models.
s5e679a7e80.why: Interpretability tools for state-space vision models are needed as these architectures move beyond transformers.

s1622bdd5ba.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science
s1622bdd5ba.description: arXiv:2611.25651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials science involves highly heterogeneous scientific information, including textual knowledge, molecular and crystal structures, experimental characterization data, microscopy images, and structure-property relationships. Developing a general-purpose foundation model capable of understanding and reasoning over these diverse materials representations remains challenging. In this technical report, we introduce MatVerse, a materials foundation model built upon Intern-S2-Preview and further specialized through large-scale materials-domain post-training. We construct a large-scale multimodal training corpus covering materials knowledge, scientific reasoning, quantitative problem solving, structural understanding, and multimodal scientific in
s1622bdd5ba.summary: Researchers introduce MatVerse, a materials science foundation model built on Intern-S2-Preview and specialized on materials-domain data.

sa75b074bac.title: Multiple Criteria Decision Making Under XORness
sa75b074bac.description: arXiv:2611.25652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How should we make decisions under XORness? XORness is a class of uncertainty arising from indeterminacy, exclusivity, and hesitancy. We develop a multiple criteria decision making framework that preserves XORness throughout the decision process. We define XOR numbers and prove their fundamental arithmetic and algebraic properties. Building on these results, we extend the deterministic decision matrix to an XOR decision matrix and introduce a compatible normalization procedure. Further, we propose an additive XOR aggregation operator, which preserves indeterminacy, exclusivity, and hesitancy inherent in evaluations. sa75b074bac.summary: Researchers develop a multiple criteria decision making framework based on XOR numbers to handle uncertainty from indeterminacy and hesitancy.

s6c61f1f18f.title: SiliconGym: A Versatile Reinforcement Learning Environment for Agentic EDA
s6c61f1f18f.description: arXiv:2611.25658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) with electronic design automation (EDA) feedback is advancing large language models for hardware design and verification. Extending these gains to hardware-engineering agents requires environments that span tasks, preserve state across tool calls, and support large hierarchies alongside parallel rollouts. We present SiliconGym, the first versatile, cross-task and cross-toolchain RL environment for hardware design and verification. By decoupling versioned workspaces, budgeted execution, and acceptance-gated scoring, SiliconGym scales from module-level RTL, testbench, and PPA tasks to multi-round repository repair and full-hierarchy SoC flows. Streaming dispatch overlaps tool checks with generation, finishing a 256-a
s6c61f1f18f.summary: Researchers present SiliconGym, a cross-task, cross-toolchain reinforcement learning environment for agentic electronic design automation.
s6c61f1f18f.why: Training hardware-design agents with EDA feedback requires stateful, parallel environments like this, which could speed up chip design automation.

sb56a0b995e.title: Ask in the Crowd: Differentially Private LLM Inference via Dummy-Augmented Shuffling
sb56a0b995e.description: arXiv:2611.25669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as LLM-as-a-Service (LLMaaS), where user queries are sent to remote LLMs for inference, raising severe privacy concerns about the exposure of sensitive user inputs. Differentially private inference mitigates these risks by injecting noise into input embeddings. However, existing methods struggle to balance privacy and utility, as stronger privacy protection often leads to substantial accuracy degradation in LLM inference. In this work, we propose DP-SPD, a differentially private LLM inference framework that protects user queries by hiding the real query among client-generated dummy queries. All queries are randomly shuffled before being sent to the server, preventing direct identification of the
sb56a0b995e.summary: Researchers propose DP-SPD, a differentially private LLM inference framework using dummy-augmented shuffling to protect user queries sent to remote models.
sb56a0b995e.why: LLM-as-a-service users risk exposing sensitive inputs, and this aims to improve the privacy-utility tradeoff over noise-injection methods.

s7364157bb2.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation
s7364157bb2.description: arXiv:2611.25670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs) requires reducing both intermediate reasoning steps and their execution cost. Latent CoT methods compress textual rationales into continuous thoughts, yet their full-precision (FP) models retain substantial storage and computation costs. Lowering numerical precision could reduce these remaining costs, yet direct quantization severely degrades reasoning accuracy, particularly with 4-bit weights and activations. Operator and perturbation analyses reveal key sensitivity and direction-dependent predictive effects of continuous-thought errors, motivating preservation of information retrieval and subsequent reasoning beyond reconstruction accuracy. We therefore introduce QL
s7364157bb2.summary: Researchers propose a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation method to make latent chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language models cheaper while preserving accuracy at low bit widths.
s7364157bb2.why: Shows a path to running multimodal reasoning models at lower precision, cutting storage and compute costs without the accuracy loss of direct 4-bit quantization.

sfd942addf7.title: LATER: Learning Action-Conditioned Temporal Evidence Retrieval for Predictive World Models
sfd942addf7.description: arXiv:2611.25671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early interactions can reveal physical properties that later observations no longer show. These properties can still gov- ern the effects of future actions. Inspired by the distinction between retention and selective readout in working mem- ory and cognitive science, we introduce LATER, an action- conditioned world model built on CF-JEPA. LATER stores completed real transitions in partitioned memories that remain fixed during candidate rollouts. A response bridge queries these memories using the current state and candidate action, while multi-cut auxiliary supervision trains the memory writ- ers. On distracted Two-Stage PushT, LATER raises terminal success from 15.5% to 25.0% over reconstructed CF-JEPA. In a separate comparison across six mod
sfd942addf7.summary: Researchers introduce LATER, an action-conditioned world model that stores past real transitions in partitioned memories and retrieves them during candidate action rollouts.
sfd942addf7.why: Suggests a way for predictive world models to recall early observations that still affect future action outcomes, relevant to robotics and planning systems.

s832fd68282.title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
s832fd68282.description: arXiv:2611.25673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As language-model agents are applied to increasingly extended tasks, their working context continuously accumulates interaction history, tool observations, intermediate decisions, and task progress. Context compaction offers a practical way to reduce this growing history while allowing execution to continue, yet the compaction ability of modern LLMs remains insufficiently understood. We introduce CompAct-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating working-context compaction through its downstream effect on agent task completion. Starting from successful agent trajectories, we insert compaction boundaries at different stages of execution, compress the preceding working context with the model under evaluation, and let the same executor continue the origi
s832fd68282.summary: Researchers release CompAct-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well LLMs compact working context and whether that preserves downstream agent task completion.
s832fd68282.why: Gives teams a way to evaluate context compaction strategies for long-running agents by their effect on task success rather than summary quality alone.

safba7c1f68.title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies
safba7c1f68.description: arXiv:2611.25695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on visual feedback throughout manipulation, making them vulnerable to persistent texture attacks. However, optimized patterns can stand out from their surroundings, making an attack easier to notice and its carrier more likely to be inspected or removed. To address this limitation, our key insight is to search the structured image distribution of a diffusion model for natural-looking textures while using closed-loop feedback to identify task-disruptive candidates. Based on this idea, we propose DMT-Attack, a gradient-free gray-box attack that generates textures for ordinary scene objects such as tablecloths. safba7c1f68.summary: Researchers propose DMT-Attack, which searches a diffusion model's texture distribution for natural-looking patterns that disrupt closed-loop vision-language-action robot policies.
safba7c1f68.why: Highlights a stealthier adversarial threat to robot manipulation policies that rely on visual feedback, relevant to securing deployed embodied AI.

sdc59546733.title: MemMend: A Selective Revision Framework for Memory Question Answering
sdc59546733.description: arXiv:2611.25721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Revising every answer from a long-term memory can consume substantial inference budget and damage facts that were already correct. We introduce MemMend, a modular selective revision framework that routes potentially incomplete answers to an editor, represents corrections as bounded exact-text replacements, and accepts only edits with resolvable source coordinates and valid edit operations. The editor preserves the current answer when no legal repair is proposed; accepted edits require no additional semantic-verification call. On 1,986 LoCoMo development questions, MemMend achieves 67.17 conversation-macro F1 and 88.35 mean Judge score, improving over a verified revision chain by 0.82 and 1.24 points while using 62.37% fewer revision calls. sdc59546733.summary: Researchers present MemMend, a selective revision framework that edits only likely-incomplete answers from long-term memory using bounded exact-text replacements.
sdc59546733.why: Offers a way to improve memory-based QA accuracy while limiting inference cost and avoiding damage to answers that were already correct.

s93a0140f86.title: ADAPT: Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing
s93a0140f86.description: arXiv:2611.25754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-based classifiers efficiently route queries to specialised services, but they typically select a candidate even when no suitable service exists. We introduce Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing (ADAPT), a lightweight routing architecture with an explicit fallback option that enables queries to abstain from specialist selection. ADAPT uses the separation between the highest relevance score and the candidate score distribution as routing confidence. s93a0140f86.summary: Researchers present ADAPT, a lightweight service-routing method that lets retrieval-based classifiers abstain from selecting a specialist when no suitable service exists.
s93a0140f86.why: Addresses a common failure in routing systems that always pick a candidate, which matters for reliable query dispatch in multi-service architectures.

s26f8186775.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
s26f8186775.description: arXiv:2611.25773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-duplex interaction models exhibit strong conversational agency, enabling natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions. However, completing tasks further requires task agency: timely tool invocation and argument revision following user corrections. Frontend-backend agents separate initiation from execution: the frontend decides whether and what to request, while the backend determines how. Execution can be offloaded, but unsent requests cannot be executed, and incomplete ones can misdirect the backend. On Full-Duplex-Bench v3 (FDB v3), most failures of Realtime-Venus-Audio + Harness in our streaming pipeline occur before a domain tool executes. We introduce Duopra, a full-duplex interaction model that learns task exec
s26f8186775.summary: Researchers propose Duopra, a frontend-backend architecture that adds task agency to full-duplex conversational models, enabling timely tool calls and argument revisions after user corrections.
s26f8186775.why: Points to a design pattern for voice agents that must act on tools mid-conversation without misdirecting backend execution.

sab7e0729ac.title: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards
sab7e0729ac.description: arXiv:2611.25793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal safety guards increasingly generate rationales alongside safety predictions, yet whether these rationales are reliable remains largely unexplored. We systematically study *rationale hallucination* from two perspectives: visual rationale hallucination, where rationales contain unsupported visual facts, and safety attribution hallucination, where grounded content is assigned an incorrect safety interpretation. Across rationale-generation methods, multiple vision-language backbones, and safety datasets, we find that rationale hallucination is widespread and does not consistently diminish with higher classification accuracy or increased model scale. sab7e0729ac.summary: Researchers study rationale hallucination in multimodal safety guard models, finding that generated explanations often include unsupported visual facts or misattributed safety interpretations.
sab7e0729ac.why: Warns teams not to trust safety classifier explanations at face value, since rationales can be unreliable even when predictions look correct.

s3e6dae0522.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing
s3e6dae0522.description: arXiv:2611.25811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many prompt-driven FLUX editing methods rely on injecting source features into target-conditioned generation, creating an inherent trade-off between source preservation and the desired edit. We address this problem by controlling where source features are injected and which transformer blocks are used. First, we introduce adaptive masks that spatially gate feature injection using differences between source- and target-conditioned block outputs at matched inversion states. Second, we use REINFORCE to select Top-K injection blocks under different preservation-editability objectives. The selected blocks are fixed at inference and require no online search. s3e6dae0522.summary: Researchers propose spatially adaptive masks and REINFORCE-based block selection to control where source features are injected in FLUX rectified-flow image editing.
s3e6dae0522.why: Offers a technique to better balance source preservation against edit strength in prompt-driven image editing pipelines.

s0779374b94.title: Anchor and Check: Deterministic Cross-Prompt, Cross-Model Reconciliation for Auditable LLM Decisions
s0779374b94.description: arXiv:2611.25818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pipelines that let a large language model (LLM) make discrete decisions need to know which decisions they may act on unattended, and a record that explains each one. We study a small, fully specified reconciliation contract: commit the target model's greedy answer (the anchor), draw one or two greedy checks that reach the answer by a different route (an alternate prompt, or a model from another family), and let a pure function return one of five outcomes, of which only Agree is acted on. s0779374b94.summary: Researchers propose a reconciliation contract that compares a greedy LLM answer against alternate-route checks and acts only when outcomes agree, evaluated on 48,000 model-item runs.
s0779374b94.why: Gives a deterministic, auditable mechanism for deciding which LLM outputs are safe to act on without human review.

s5353113a01.title: Whose Risks Count? What 1,901 AI Incidents Reveal About Corporate Disclosures
s5353113a01.description: arXiv:2611.25841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems can harm people, yet the AI actors that provide or deploy them are rarely obliged to disclose these risks. US securities regulation is an exception. Companies registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) must disclose their material risks, including those of their AI systems, in filings that carry liability for misstatement. Materiality, however, is defined by what a reasonable investor would consider important, so harms to third parties enter disclosure only insofar as they become financial risks for the company. We test whether AI harms do so by matching 9,001 AI incidents to 18,229 SEC filings of 328 AI actors by risk type. s5353113a01.summary: A study of 1,901 AI incidents examines whether US SEC-registered companies disclose AI-related risks, noting that third-party harms enter filings only when they become financial risks.
s5353113a01.why: Signals how securities disclosure rules may shape what AI risks companies report, relevant to compliance and risk teams.

s2b2254978d.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents
s2b2254978d.description: arXiv:2611.25855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized LLM agents must act on a user's current preferences, which change across interactions and are rarely stated in full. Existing memory systems store and retrieve content from the interaction history and leave the agent to work out which preferences still hold and where they apply. Such content does not indicate whether a preference is still current or where it applies, so agents often act on outdated or misapplied preferences. We instead treat memory as the assistant's belief about the user. s2b2254978d.summary: Researchers introduce HabitusMem, a memory approach that treats stored content as an agent's belief about evolving user preferences, tracking whether preferences are current and where they apply.
s2b2254978d.why: Suggests a memory design for personalized agents that avoids acting on outdated or misapplied user preferences.

sf3066722a4.title: Decoupled Knowledge Retrieval and Compact Memory Enable Reliable Lifelong Model Editing
sf3066722a4.description: arXiv:2611.25861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lifelong model editing requires continuously incorporating new facts into deployed large language models (LLMs) without expensive retraining or compromising existing capabilities. Memory-based editors offer an appealing solution by keeping the base parameters untouched, yet their practical use is hindered by linearly growing storage requirements and deteriorating retrieval performance as edits accumulate. To tackle these problems, we introduce BiSpace, a lifelong model editing framework that decouples memory retrieval from knowledge injection across two distinct representation spaces. sf3066722a4.summary: Researchers propose BiSpace, a lifelong model editing framework that decouples memory retrieval from knowledge injection to limit storage growth and retrieval degradation as edits accumulate.
sf3066722a4.why: Addresses scaling problems in memory-based LLM editors, relevant for keeping deployed models updated with new facts over time.

s5072ff5659.title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
s5072ff5659.description: arXiv:2611.25868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible. s5072ff5659.summary: Researchers present StarTV-Agent, a tool-augmented vision-language agent that combines policy learning with experience evolution for traffic scenario understanding.
s5072ff5659.why: Shows how persistent tool orchestration and experience reuse may reduce repeated planning cost in multi-tool vision agents.

s6273445c75.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
s6273445c75.description: arXiv:2611.25879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The occurrence of echo chambers is a well-known phenomenon in social networks. Echo chambers are groups of agents satisfying three properties: homogeneity, i.e., sharing the same opinion, segregation, i.e., listening primarily to agents of the same group, and reinforcement, i.e., increasing opinion similarity over time. Opinion dynamics models have been used to explain how echo chambers occur through agents updating their opinions. However, social network users also exchange beliefs supporting their opinions. Here, we aim at identifying the effect of propagating beliefs together with opinions on the formation of echo chambers. s6273445c75.summary: A corrected paper models how coherent belief and opinion propagation in social networks can produce more echo chambers than opinion dynamics alone.
s6273445c75.why: Offers limited direct relevance to engineering work, though it may inform modeling of recommendation-driven polarization.

s68bddc4248.title: Trustworthy Geospatial AI Workflows: Reproducible Maritime Analytics and Forecasting on Open-Source AIS Data
s68bddc4248.description: arXiv:2611.25884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Publicly available geospatial data provide increasing opportuni- ties for data-driven maritime analytics and predictive modelling. However, their availability does not necessarily imply that the underlying observations are equally suitable for downstream AI applications. Properties of the data source and observation pro- cess, including provenance, reporting regularity, spatial coverage, observation density, and missingness, can affect how geospatial data are interpreted, processed, and ultimately used by predictive models. At the same time, trustworthy geospatial AI requires ana- lytical workflows in which these processing decisions can be made explicit and reproduced. s68bddc4248.summary: A paper proposes reproducible geospatial AI workflows for maritime analytics and forecasting using open-source AIS data, focusing on data provenance, coverage, and missingness.
s68bddc4248.why: Engineers using public geospatial datasets must check provenance, reporting regularity, and missingness before trusting downstream predictive models.

s1c37600d73.title: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization
s1c37600d73.description: arXiv:2611.25891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models enable agents to optimize RTL using EDA feedback, yet their executable search procedures remain largely hand- engineered. We present Meta-RTL, an EDA-grounded framework that evolves RTL optimization harnesses from a minimal loop while keeping the optimization model, EDA flow, and per-design budgets fixed. Compared with Dr. RTL, Meta-RTL* reduces aggregate WNS/TNS violations by 7.8%/11.0% across 20 development designs, with area reductions on 70% of them. s1c37600d73.summary: Meta-RTL is a framework that evolves agent harnesses for RTL optimization using EDA feedback, reporting reduced WNS/TNS violations versus Dr. RTL on development designs.
s1c37600d73.why: It suggests LLM agents can automate hand-engineered hardware design search loops, with results reported on both development and unseen designs.

sfa15f0bcba.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
sfa15f0bcba.description: arXiv:2611.25894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. sfa15f0bcba.summary: A paper reviews ML methods for solar PV power forecasting and sets out a reproducible workflow combining automated model selection with explainability.
sfa15f0bcba.why: It addresses common flaws in forecasting evaluation, such as random splits and missing reference forecasts, that make published accuracy hard to compare.

s366a6210ac.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
s366a6210ac.description: arXiv:2611.25895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion language models typically use a fixed denoising schedule across workloads. We show that the cheapest schedule that preserves quality depends on the task, model, and sampler. s366a6210ac.summary: Researchers propose TCDA, a method that selects the cheapest diffusion language model denoising schedule certified to preserve quality, using bootstrap bounds.
s366a6210ac.why: It offers a deployment rule with an explicit error guarantee for reducing inference cost of diffusion language models without quality loss.

s1d20fb5d0a.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
s1d20fb5d0a.description: arXiv:2611.25896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a \emph{verifiable artifact}: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. se0d06fe12d.title: From Cases to Criteria: Reusing Evaluation Knowledge for Task-Specific Rubric Generation
se0d06fe12d.description: arXiv:2611.25903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Query-specific rubrics make LLM evaluation more fine-grained and transparent, and generating high-quality rubrics requires both identifying the target query's evaluation scope and specifying concrete checks. Historical rubrics provide reusable evaluation experiences, yet existing approaches reuse either complete query-rubric cases or aggregated criteria and dimensions without explicitly connecting recurring evaluation requirements to their criterion-level evidence and source-query context. se0d06fe12d.summary: A paper proposes reusing criterion-level evaluation knowledge from historical rubrics to generate task-specific rubrics for LLM evaluation.
se0d06fe12d.why: Better rubric generation could make LLM evaluation more fine-grained and transparent, though the summary gives limited implementation detail.

sb27a4fdeb6.title: Validation-driven Deployment of LLM Inference Platforms for Agentic Workloads
sb27a4fdeb6.description: arXiv:2611.25905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprises are moving agentic workloads from closed APIs to their own open-weight model deployments. We present an end-to-end evaluation pipeline for agentic LLM serving and empirically ground the design choices that connect its stages. sb27a4fdeb6.summary: Researchers present an end-to-end evaluation pipeline for validating open-weight LLM inference deployments serving agentic workloads, including trace replay.
sb27a4fdeb6.why: Enterprises moving agent workloads to self-hosted open-weight models need validation from testing through production sizing, and replayed traces can reproduce session behavior.

sc05b414a1b.title: ROAM-GRPO: Enforcing Reasoning Diversity in GRPO via Routed Off-mode Approach Mining
sc05b414a1b.description: arXiv:2611.25926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) paired with Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has become the dominant recipe for post-training LLMs on complex reasoning tasks, but has been shown to collapse the policy into a low-diversity mode. Repeated LLM outputs are nearly identical, and pass@k accuracy converges or degrades as a result. We propose ROAM-GRPO (Routed Off-mode Approach Mining for GRPO), an augmentation to the GRPO algorithm which incentivizes exploration of distinct reasoning strategies and aims to increase output creativity during evaluation. ROAM-GRPO detects well-solved problems during training and transfers them to an "off-mode" track. The model is prompted to produce distinct solution strategies to such problems, which
sc05b414a1b.summary: ROAM-GRPO augments GRPO with routed off-mode approach mining to encourage diverse reasoning strategies and counter output collapse after SFT and RLVR.
sc05b414a1b.why: Reduced output diversity hurts pass@k accuracy in reasoning post-training, so this offers a training technique to address it.

sf690c2e11c.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport
sf690c2e11c.description: arXiv:2611.25950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate surface modeling of multi-transparent interfaces to achieve accurate light transmission. The interplay of errors in geometric structure, light paths, and observation results during the reconstruction of transparent media with a high number of layers makes this a challenging problem. Some existing techniques address the reconstruction of transparent scenes by reducing the number of layers or simplifying light paths; however, this limits their direct applicability to high-order transparent scenes. We propose GaussTrans, a compact framework for light transport in high-order transparent scenes, consisting of three components: Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces, Transport-Coupled Refinement, and Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection. G
sf690c2e11c.summary: GaussTrans is a Gaussian interface framework for modeling light transmission through multi-layer transparent surfaces and reconstructing high-layer transparent scenes.
sf690c2e11c.why: The text gives little on applications or results for engineering teams beyond the reconstruction problem it targets.

s9ba985a705.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
s9ba985a705.description: arXiv:2611.25991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crash simulations of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts are highly sensitive to the fiber-orientation field supplied to the material model. In conventional workflows, that field comes from resin-flow analysis, which requires molding-specialist support and takes about 25 hours of work per part. We previously proposed a surrogate model that addresses this bottleneck by predicting the orientation field in about 3 minutes. This paper reports the implementation, validation, and operational design that turned the model into an engineering tool for Honda design workflows. We present staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, evaluation against a predefined engineering angular-error criterion, and the expert review that approved design u
s9ba985a705.summary: Authors report turning an AI surrogate that predicts glass-fiber orientation in about 3 minutes into an engineering tool for crash CAE workflows, replacing about 25 hours of resin-flow work per part.
s9ba985a705.why: Shows a production path for ML surrogates in simulation pipelines, replacing a costly specialist-dependent step with a validated tool.

sb1bf002e54.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
sb1bf002e54.description: arXiv:2611.26003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. sb1bf002e54.summary: A paper reports AI agents can redesign engineering parts with over a thousand CAD parameters while coordinating with nonlinear finite-element simulations.
sb1bf002e54.why: Agentic optimization could handle high-dimensional CAD design where classical optimizers need manual setup, relevant to simulation-driven engineering teams.

scf4ecfeeed.title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
scf4ecfeeed.description: arXiv:2611.26007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. Inspired by coached motor learning, this paper presents System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which couples two loops. The high-frequency online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle: a decision model maps each visual observation and task question to structured judgments, and a decision tree converts them into timed actions without invoking a reasoning model. scf4ecfeeed.summary: System-One RSI couples a fast OODA decision loop with recursive self-improvement to help interactive agents learn sub-second control from guided practice.
scf4ecfeeed.why: Targets the latency gap where reasoning models are too slow for real-time control, a constraint for interactive agent deployments.

s957ccde0dd.title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing
s957ccde0dd.description: arXiv:2611.26012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating whether artificial agents behave like humans requires comparing not just average outcomes but entire behavioral distributions across diverse contexts. We propose a stratified framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells, and discovers subgroup rules identifying where agent behavior departs from human play. We show that session-level metrics dominated by win/loss outcomes offer little signal beyond mean comparisons, whereas process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal genuine behavioral differences. s957ccde0dd.summary: Researchers propose a stratified conditional distributional testing framework to locate where agent behavior diverges from human play, using process-level metrics.
s957ccde0dd.why: Outcome metrics like win/loss gave little signal, so process metrics such as move efficiency are needed to evaluate agents against humans.

s36477a3f9f.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
s36477a3f9f.description: arXiv:2611.26024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-form video understanding, as a fundamental yet crucial vision task, is being revolutionized by multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based video agents. However, the retrieval-driven nature inherent to these agents creates a significant bottleneck, forcing them to reactively fetch clips based on local saliency without a global temporal plan. To address this, we present ForeSeek, a foresight-driven video agent that transforms long-video reasoning from reactive retrieval into predictive exploration. Rather than blindly probing the timeline, ForeSeek forms visually grounded expectations over unseen temporal regions, verifies them through targeted observations, and continuously refines its search based on emerging evidence, where failed exp
s36477a3f9f.summary: ForeSeek is a video agent that uses foresight-driven planning to shift long-form video understanding from reactive clip retrieval to predictive exploration.
s36477a3f9f.why: Addresses a retrieval bottleneck in MLLM video agents by adding a global temporal plan, though the text gives no benchmark figures.

s5a1d88c3ac.title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions
s5a1d88c3ac.description: arXiv:2611.26029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate item probabilities can produce inaccurate group-level decisions. A system may score each item separately, yet act on whether enough hidden items succeed: show a slate, defer a panel decision, or inspect a batch. When items share an uncertain latent state, independent marginalization preserves means but removes dependence from the aggregate posterior. We call this error the serialization tax. s5a1d88c3ac.summary: The paper defines a serialization tax: scoring shared-latent items independently yields accurate marginals but misstates group-level decision distributions.
s5a1d88c3ac.why: Engineers making batch or panel decisions from per-item probabilities may get systematically wrong aggregate risk if items share a latent state.

sef210e1d36.title: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines
sef210e1d36.description: arXiv:2611.26033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Camera-equipped glasses can convert an examination page into a query to a vision-language model (VLM). Device detection addresses possession; a complementary question is whether an examination document can reduce the usefulness of an unauthorized capture. We present SEOYUN, an application-specific framework for refusal-inducing exam documents, with optical and encoder-level interventions as extensions. We use reverse jailbreaking to describe the direction of the objective: inducing abstention rather than bypassing refusal. Refusal induction and defensive visual prompt injection already have precedents; our contribution is a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol for examination use. We distinguish refusal from correct-ans
sef210e1d36.summary: Researchers propose SEOYUN, a framework for exam documents designed to induce AI models to refuse answering when photographed by camera glasses.
sef210e1d36.why: It explores document-level defenses against unauthorized VLM capture of exam content, though the abstract gives limited detail on effectiveness.

sc12364fa44.title: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face
sc12364fa44.description: arXiv:2611.26050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) entered into force in August 2024, and its obligations apply in stages. Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models have applied since August 2025, and transparency rules since August 2026. These obligations affect developers who share and deploy models and applications on public platforms such as Hugging Face (HF), the largest platform for distributing AI artifacts. However, little is known about how practitioners respond to the regulation in practice. To address this gap, we conducted an empirical study of explicit references to the AI Act on HF. We collected over five million records, including repository cards, discussions, and commits from Models, Datasets, and Spaces,
sc12364fa44.summary: A study examines how the EU AI Act is referenced across Hugging Face, looking at how practitioners respond to the regulation on a major model-sharing platform.
sc12364fa44.why: Engineers publishing models on public platforms may face AI Act transparency and provider obligations, and this shows early practitioner responses.

s495c38cf97.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
s495c38cf97.description: arXiv:2611.26074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear
s495c38cf97.summary: Researchers train a biologically inspired spiking neural network to control the Unitree H1-2 humanoid robot in locomotion tasks, tested in simulation.

s8ff3429a3d.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors
s8ff3429a3d.description: arXiv:2611.26108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study data-sharing among firms competing in the same market through the quality of their predictive models. We model firms' profit through two main components, precision and market share, where the former depends on the firm's own number of datapoints and the latter depends on the endowments of all firms. We characterize Pareto-optimal contracts as those in which at least one firm receives all of the other firms' datapoints. We then propose a parametric family of data-sharing contracts and show that, under any of them, the relative market shares of all firms remain constant, eliminating the negative effect of sharing data with competitors and equalizing all firms' gains relative to the no-sharing scenario. s8ff3429a3d.summary: A paper studies data-sharing between competing firms, characterizing Pareto-optimal contracts and proposing a strategyproof parametric family of data-sharing contracts.
s8ff3429a3d.why: Teams weighing data partnerships with competitors can use these incentive results to reason about contract design, though the work is theoretical.

s39ffc4e1e0.title: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs
s39ffc4e1e0.description: arXiv:2611.26109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active urban sensing orchestrates a mobile sensor fleet to proactively inspect a dynamic road network and gather critical information for system management. This problem simultaneously requires understanding the complex spatio-temporal evolution and making decisions with partial observations. In this work, we focus on active sensing in a large-scale urban road network with utilities grounded in dynamic traffic states, while prior work has rarely considered these factors jointly. We propose \emph{SenseAlign}, a Reinforcement Learning-based (RL) framework that learns decision-aligned predictive representations for coordinating an urban sensing drone fleet. SenseAlign first trains a privileged teacher agent that exploits future ground-truth traf
s39ffc4e1e0.summary: SenseAlign is a reinforcement learning framework for coordinating UAV sensor fleets to actively sense dynamic urban road networks under partial observations.

s4bcf6edde4.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
s4bcf6edde4.description: arXiv:2611.26132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training recursive self-improvement (RSI) iteratively improves a target capability, operationalized by a fixed anchor benchmark, through repeated intervention, training, and evaluation. Yet most loops use the anchor's aggregate score as their sole observation, so early gains give way to stalled progress and repetitive exploration. When this anchor-only feedback ceases to reveal actionable gaps, a plateau may reflect an exhausted observation rather than an exhausted capability.
