s4bcf6edde4.summary: Sage-Evolve-Preview introduces adaptive observation (AdaObs), a method that varies the feedback signals used in post-training self-improvement loops to avoid plateaus.
s4bcf6edde4.why: Richer feedback signals than a single aggregate benchmark score may help teams break stalls in iterative model post-training loops.

sc0a18809d1.title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
sc0a18809d1.description: arXiv:2611.26171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operations research (OR) relies on algorithms that experts tailor to each problem: a new routing, scheduling or network design problem can take weeks of specialist work before it is solved well at scale. Large language model (LLM) agents now write, test and improve code, but whether they can design algorithms that scale to realistic instances is open: in the FrontierOR benchmark's one-shot evaluation, the strongest model matches Gurobi, with an objective within 1% of Gurobi's and no slower, on only 39% of the large instances. The FrontierOR Challenge asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems, spanning six a
sc0a18809d1.summary: The FrontierOR Challenge invites agentic LLM systems to design operations research algorithms, benchmarked against Gurobi on large problem instances.
sc0a18809d1.why: It benchmarks whether LLM agents can produce scalable optimization algorithms, a useful signal for teams considering agents for operations research workloads.

s16786d1175.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
s16786d1175.description: arXiv:2611.26235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. s16786d1175.summary: Researchers use physics-informed features and pretrained tabular foundation models to predict melt pool geometry in laser powder bed fusion manufacturing.
s16786d1175.why: Pretrained tabular models with physics-informed features may reduce data needs for process modeling in advanced manufacturing.

sddeb13a691.title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
sddeb13a691.description: arXiv:2611.26248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduce TwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences, and engineering. sddeb13a691.summary: TwinLab-Bench is a benchmark that evaluates AI scientist agents by having them execute self-designed experiments grounded in readings from a real laboratory.

s877789619f.title: Similarity-based OSF Logic for Flexible SPARQL Query Answering
s877789619f.description: arXiv:2611.26261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an updated version of fosf, a reasoner for fuzzy order-sorted feature (OSF) logic, with support for flexible SPARQL query answering over RDF knowledge graphs. Fuzzy OSF logic is a knowledge representation and reasoning language where feature symbols denote functions and sort symbols denote fuzzy sets. Sorts are organized in a fuzzy subsumption relation that extends to OSF terms, record-like structures representing classes of entities. s877789619f.summary: An updated fosf reasoner adds flexible SPARQL query answering over RDF knowledge graphs using similarity-based fuzzy order-sorted feature logic.

se531a5ed1b.title: Client Exits - A Way to Increase LLM Transparency on the Client Side
se531a5ed1b.description: arXiv:2611.26309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Textual recommendations generated by large language models (LLMs) can be difficult to inspect. This paper introduces \emph{Client Exits}, a lightweight mechanism for enriching LLM responses while separating semantic intent from client-specific presentation. The model inserts predefined, machine-interpretable markers into its output, and the receiving client decides whether and how to realize the corresponding enrichments. This allows supplementary information to be presented as graphics, text, speech, or other modalities without prescribing a concrete interface. se531a5ed1b.summary: Client Exits is a proposed mechanism where LLMs insert machine-interpretable markers into output, letting clients decide how to render supplementary enrichments.
se531a5ed1b.why: Separating semantic intent from presentation could make LLM recommendations easier to inspect and render across client modalities.

sb167e34972.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
sb167e34972.description: arXiv:2611.26313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. Existing methods often transform logic formulas into automata for state augmentation and reward shaping. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. sb167e34972.summary: Actor-Predictor is a reinforcement learning framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress to enforce formal specifications without building automata.
sb167e34972.why: It offers a way to handle temporal safety constraints in RL without automaton construction, which limits existing methods to small specifications.

s097807cc47.title: Rigel-Ladon: An Option-Count Law for a One-Pass Decision Encoder, Tested on Held-Out Option Counts and Held-Out Schemas
s097807cc47.description: arXiv:2611.26332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is a small neural network that reads a text, a question and K written options, and returns one probability per option in a single pass. s097807cc47.summary: Rigel-Ladon studies how the accuracy of Laya, a small one-pass neural decision encoder, falls as the number of answer options grows from 2 to 35.

s149ee90286.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
s149ee90286.description: arXiv:2611.26335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) often answer questions from incomplete records. Missing information might be interpreted as unknown or false, depending on the completeness of the source. s149ee90286.why: Agents answering from incomplete records need to handle missing data correctly, and this benchmark isolates that behavior from other reasoning demands.

s42decf3fa9.title: Sirius-Tiamat: How Small Can a One-Pass Decision Encoder Get Before Its Decisions Change?
s42decf3fa9.description: arXiv:2611.26339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A one-pass decision encoder reads a text, a question and several named options, and returns a probability for each option in a single forward pass. s42decf3fa9.why: Quantifying how far small decision encoders can be compressed before outputs shift informs edge deployment trade-offs.

s8446d0ac05.title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits
s8446d0ac05.description: arXiv:2611.26342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly rely on extended reasoning traces, yet the training signals used to shape this behavior remain coarse. Supervised fine-tuning on full trajectories forces the model to imitate an entire demonstration, overconstraining its output distribution, while trajectory-level reinforcement learning provides only weak credit assignment, rewarding or penalizing whole completions without identifying where they succeed or fail. s8446d0ac05.why: It offers finer-grained credit assignment than full-trajectory SFT or trajectory-level RL, which may help shape reasoning behavior more precisely.

sf16d2a6d81.title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
sf16d2a6d81.description: arXiv:2611.26343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automating experiments does not necessarily advance scientific understanding. sf16d2a6d81.summary: Researchers introduce DeepQuest, an AI scientist framework that turns Alzheimer's knowledge gaps into testable hypotheses, prioritizes them, and runs iterative experiments.
sf16d2a6d81.why: It shows a research-agent design that prioritizes hypotheses by knowledge gaps and data feasibility, not just automated experiment volume.

se2456af9ac.title: Context as a Resource
se2456af9ac.description: arXiv:2611.26346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Managing concurrent tasks across separate agent sessions quickly exhausts human attention, motivating always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface. Conversely, router-ticket hierarchies incur lossy prose handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges - collapsing true-conflict repository merges to a 33.3% three-run mean despite high isolated branch passes. se2456af9ac.why: It highlights architectural tradeoffs in managing concurrent agent tasks, though the text gives limited detail on the proposed solution.

sc5f0a27c00.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
sc5f0a27c00.description: arXiv:2611.26361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. sc5f0a27c00.summary: A paper describes a pipeline where LLM agents mine lessons from their own trajectories, consolidate them into guidelines, and use them at inference, with deployment lessons on memory size.
sc5f0a27c00.why: Engineers building long-horizon agents can learn how much memory to inject at inference and how to consolidate self-generated lessons.

s68ae11985f.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
s68ae11985f.description: arXiv:2611.26366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. s68ae11985f.why: Shows that world models may ignore observed evidence in favor of learned priors, a risk for cross-environment physical prediction.

s335988aa8d.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
s335988aa8d.description: arXiv:2611.26414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. s335988aa8d.summary: ZeroVLN proposes a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain fine-tuning of the VLM brain, preserving general visual capabilities.
s335988aa8d.why: Suggests navigation agents can use frozen VLMs without degrading general visual abilities, a useful pattern for embodied AI teams.

s874cd7311c.title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
s874cd7311c.description: arXiv:2611.26422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate Q-matrices for diagnostic classification models that approximate expert specifications, but evaluations have focused on the final matrices, leaving the basis of individual item-attribute assignments unexamined. This opacity limits the responsible use of AI in measurement. We propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis (RTA), a framework in which an LLM generates attribute-labeled reasoning steps through chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and these steps are analyzed to reconstruct, compare, and inspect each assignment. s874cd7311c.summary: Researchers propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis, using attribute-labeled chain-of-thought steps from LLMs to inspect and explain item-attribute assignments in Q-matrix construction.
s874cd7311c.why: Offers a way to audit LLM-generated assessment structures, which matters for responsible AI use in educational measurement.

s509ad10ed8.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
s509ad10ed8.description: arXiv:2611.26423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep-research agents repeatedly decide what to search, read, and verify, often using large cloud-hosted language models for action proposal. However, privacy and local control motivate running agents on users' devices, where limited memory and compute favor smaller models and complicate on-device training. Yet inference-time guidance faces three obstacles: exploring alternatives through real execution adds tool calls, prompted self-evaluation is bounded by the agent's judgment, and model-specific guidance risks repeated adaptation costs. We introduce Seer, an inference-time framework providing local guidance that separates the agent's action proposal from learned consequence prediction and value estimation. From a shared corpus of real resear
s509ad10ed8.summary: Seer proposes shared decision models to guide small deep-research agents running on user devices, addressing cost and limits of inference-time guidance.
s509ad10ed8.why: Points to a route for running capable research agents locally with privacy, though details on results are not in the summary.

s5c7e324ff7.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
s5c7e324ff7.description: arXiv:2611.26450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. s5c7e324ff7.summary: A paper introduces zero-gradient circuit-grafting that compiles exact multi-digit arithmetic circuits directly into pretrained LM weights without training examples or runtime hooks.
s5c7e324ff7.why: Suggests deterministic computation can be embedded in model weights, though whether it generalizes beyond arithmetic is unclear from the text.

sdc3f594d9b.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
sdc3f594d9b.description: arXiv:2611.26464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to m
sdc3f594d9b.summary: Researchers present Monte Carlo Pass Search, which evaluates set-piece deliveries as distributions over executions and futures using a world model of soccer.

s96e8637907.title: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance
s96e8637907.description: arXiv:2611.26491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time task guidance is inherently flexible: when an agent guides a user through a task, multiple responses and timings can be appropriate, and sometimes the best action is to remain silent. Existing benchmarks often miss this flexibility by treating synthesized dialogues as fixed targets for what to say and when to say it. We introduce FLUID (Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance), a unified framework for modeling, evaluating, and enabling flexible interaction in multimodal task guidance. Using naturally occurring human-human guidance from WTaG and HoloAssist, FLUID grounds interventions in their supporting evidence, necessity, and timing flexibility, and uses this representation both to evaluate flexible guidance and to buil
s96e8637907.summary: Researchers introduce FLUID, a framework for flexible, evidence-grounded real-time task guidance that models when an agent should speak or stay silent.
s96e8637907.why: Highlights that benchmarks treating dialogues as fixed targets miss valid response variation in multimodal guidance agents.

sd0ec6f167f.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
sd0ec6f167f.description: arXiv:2611.26509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it. We investigate this question with \textbf{GLiDE}, a family of decision models spanning 0.4B to 27B parameters. Building on Qwen hybrid language models, GLiDE enables bidirectional interactions between the context, question, and candidate answers by removing causal masking from full-attention layers. To transfer reasoning capabilities into single-pass inference, we combine soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a
sd0ec6f167f.summary: GLiDE is a family of decision models from 0.4B to 27B parameters, distilled from reasoning teachers to score answers in one forward pass with calibrated confidence.
sd0ec6f167f.why: Offers a way to retain reasoning-quality decisions without generation costs, relevant for latency-sensitive decision pipelines.

s8c220fcdc7.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
s8c220fcdc7.description: arXiv:2611.26538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into thes
s8c220fcdc7.summary: The paper argues common LLM bias audits flag intersectional subgroups that independent attributes already explain, and tests a separated-interaction criterion on 150 synthetic cases.
s8c220fcdc7.why: Teams auditing model fairness may be misreading intersectional bias unless they separate interaction effects from additive effects.

s112c7e413f.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
s112c7e413f.description: arXiv:2611.26545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about
s112c7e413f.summary: Researchers test label-free persona directions from role-play to detect lies in 70B LLMs, including lies about knowledge, finding transfer works on three of four models but fails on Qwen.
s112c7e413f.why: Lie-detection probes that transfer across lie types could improve model safety monitoring, but results vary by model family.

s394a6d211b.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
s394a6d211b.description: arXiv:2611.26557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior in separate settings, leaving no common protocol to compare multimodal decision models with their backbones on practical tasks. We introduce \textbf{MM-SystemOneBias}, which evaluates 13 models on 5,323 original instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image
s394a6d211b.summary: MM-SystemOneBias is a protocol for evaluating bias in multimodal decision models, comparing them with their backbones on practical moderation and quality-judgment tasks.
s394a6d211b.why: Gives teams a common way to check whether multimodal decision models keep judgments stable across presentation changes.

sd0717acd77.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
sd0717acd77.description: arXiv:2611.26586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. sd0717acd77.summary: Researchers present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework using ProtoVAE to encode multi-layer RGBA designs into one shared spatial prototype plus one vector per layer.
sd0717acd77.why: Representation size no longer grows with cumulative layer extent, which could make generative editing of layered graphic designs more efficient.

sdbefb9b7e6.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
sdbefb9b7e6.description: arXiv:2611.26590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computat
sdbefb9b7e6.summary: Researchers introduce MC-Lens, a multimodal Jacobian lens, to probe how vision-language models select and integrate concept information in line with global workspace theory.

s84d8563609.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
s84d8563609.description: arXiv:2611.26624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. s84d8563609.summary: PlayCraft is an automated framework in which a vision-based agent plays generated games and uses its play experience to revise them for mastery and engagement.
s84d8563609.why: It shows agents can iteratively test and refine AI-generated products using their own play experience, a pattern applicable to automated design loops.

sa795e46023.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
sa795e46023.description: arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this
sa795e46023.summary: The paper argues that the tempting analogy between LLM generated token count and classical time complexity does not hold, and disproves the hypothesis tested.
sa795e46023.why: Engineers using token count as a cost proxy should be cautious, since the paper finds the analogy to classical time complexity fails.

s16ff4aab8e.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
s16ff4aab8e.description: arXiv:2611.24963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Do standard benchmarks see the architectural differences that matter? We study it with 64 from-scratch pretraining runs of Transformers and three linear-model families at 1.3-8B parameters on 1-2T Nemotron-CC tokens, at a cost of roughly 100k USD per 8B run. In academic-scale pretraining (1.3B parameters, 100B tokens), architectural differences can all but disappear when the models are carefully tuned. Instead, at 1-2T tokens they become measurable: Canon layers, which add local token mixing, consistently improve Transformers, saving about 30% of pretraining tokens for the same MMLU accuracy at 8B. s16ff4aab8e.summary: A study of 64 from-scratch Transformer and linear-model pretraining runs at 1.3-8B parameters finds Canon layers consistently improve Transformers at 1-2T tokens, saving about 30% compute.
s16ff4aab8e.why: Architectural differences that vanish at academic scale become measurable at trillion-token scale, so benchmark comparisons at small scale may mislead model architecture choices.

sbc5ae8bd09.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
sbc5ae8bd09.description: arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. sbc5ae8bd09.summary: PRKV is a training-free KV cache eviction method that estimates global token importance using Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs.
sbc5ae8bd09.why: It offers a way to cut long-context LLM KV cache memory without modifying the model, a key inference bottleneck.

s7bc95b891a.title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
s7bc95b891a.description: arXiv:2611.24970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. Evaluation of 18 closed and open-weight LLMs across ~100,00
s7bc95b891a.summary: HireWatch is an evaluation of whether LLMs comply with U.S. employment law by selecting lawful and unlawful interview questions from a 200-item bank.
s7bc95b891a.why: Teams deploying LLMs in hiring pipelines face legal compliance risk that standard evaluations do not measure.

s6a52661ada.title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
s6a52661ada.description: arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. s6a52661ada.summary: The paper studies whether a fixed in-context learning token budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or many shorter ones.
s6a52661ada.why: Prompt construction under token budgets directly affects inference cost and latency, which matters for production deployments.

s2789a3dd3f.title: No-Harm-Jury A Jury-Based Multi-Dimensional Harm Evaluation Framework for Medical AI Responses
s2789a3dd3f.description: arXiv:2611.24972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present No-Harm-Jury, a jury-based automated evaluation framework that scores AI-generated medical responses across seven conceptually distinct harm dimensions using a panel of five diverse language models as independent jurors. Responses generated by Ministral-14B on 3,000 questions drawn from PubMedQA, MedQA, and MedMCQA are scored by five jurors across dimensions of informational, social, psychological, autonomy, economic, privacy, and epistemic harm; the 151 empty responses (98 MedQA, 53 MedM- CQA) are excluded, leaving 2,849 valid samples. s2789a3dd3f.summary: No-Harm-Jury is a jury-based framework that scores AI medical responses across seven harm dimensions, using five language models as independent jurors on 3,000 questions.
s2789a3dd3f.why: It offers a multi-dimensional automated method for evaluating harm in medical AI outputs, though its reliability beyond this setup is not established here.

s21ca88d459.title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
s21ca88d459.description: arXiv:2611.24977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. While local CUAs feature robust baseline proficiency in single-step action prediction, they frequently fail at critical junctions due to rigid action loops or premature DONE decisions. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. s21ca88d459.summary: CANDID is an execution-control framework that aims to improve reliability of local computer-use agents in resource-constrained settings by addressing rigid action loops and premature DONE decisions.
s21ca88d459.why: It targets known failure modes of local computer-use agents, relevant to teams running agents on limited hardware.

s89760b18fe.title: Trace2ST: Recovering PLC Structured Text from I/O Traces with LLM Generation and Verification
s89760b18fe.description: arXiv:2611.24979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable logic controllers (PLCs), the industrial computers that operate power and process plants, often run programs whose source code is no longer available; however, every input and output of the controller is logged continuously. This paper therefore asks whether a large language model (LLM) can recover an executable program in Structured Text (ST), the standard PLC language of IEC 61131-3, from such input/output records (traces) alone and, equally important, how the recovered program can be verified. s89760b18fe.summary: Trace2ST studies whether an LLM can recover executable IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PLC programs from logged input/output traces, with a verification approach.
s89760b18fe.why: Recovering lost PLC source code from I/O logs could help industrial teams maintain legacy control systems, though the verification results are not described here.

sf8c01d79a1.title: DL101 The Representation Capability of Neural Network Models
sf8c01d79a1.description: arXiv:2611.24980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal approximation theorems (Cybenko, Funahashi, Hornik & Leshno) provide the mathematical justification for why neural networks are powerful enough to model complex, nonlinear phenomena. Shallow networks can approximate any continuous function on compact sets. Leshno's theorem clarified that non-polynomial activations are necessary for universality, which explains why ReLU, logistic, hyperbolic tangent, and other common activations work (but pure polynomials do not). However, approximation theorems provide no efficiency, training, nor generalization guarantees. sf8c01d79a1.summary: A tutorial explains the representation capability of neural networks, covering universal approximation theorems and the role of non-polynomial activations.

s138a3ed9e0.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
s138a3ed9e0.description: arXiv:2611.24994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. s138a3ed9e0.summary: Researchers use a natural-language autoencoder to translate Gemma-3-27B activations into text, letting a judge read the model's verbalized internal state to detect manipulations hidden in answers.
s138a3ed9e0.why: Monitoring internal verbalized states may catch manipulated clinical LLM outputs that look ordinary, a safety approach beyond input and output filtering.

sb2f70a7336.title: On the Impact of Feature Reduction Techniques on Adversarial Attacks
sb2f70a7336.description: arXiv:2611.25004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adversarial attacks have posed significant threats to machine learning models by exploiting their inherent vulnerabilities. Researchers have established an interdisciplinary field called adversarial machine learning to explore these vulnerabilities and develop corresponding defense strategies. Feature reduction strategies are used to decrease the dimensionality of the data in order to reduce training time, avoid the curse of dimensionality, prevent overfitting, and mitigate redundant features. However, their effect on adversarial robustness across different classifiers and attack scenarios remains insufficiently explored. sb2f70a7336.summary: The paper examines how feature reduction techniques affect the adversarial robustness of machine learning models against adversarial attacks.
sb2f70a7336.why: Dimensionality reduction used for efficiency may change model vulnerability to attacks, a factor to consider in secured ML pipelines.

sfc507974ac.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
sfc507974ac.description: arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way. sfc507974ac.summary: The paper presents near-quadratic sample compression schemes for all VC classes, addressing the long-open Floyd and Warmuth sample compression conjecture.

s5f27fb5aeb.title: DVBench: End-to-End Benchmark for Real-World UVM Design Verification Agents
s5f27fb5aeb.description: arXiv:2611.25066v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Design verification (DV) remains a major bottleneck in hardware development, with large-scale verification using the Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) being highly labor-intensive. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems offer new opportunities for DV automation. However, existing benchmarks primarily construct mutually decoupled subtasks, which deviates from the real-world workflow. In this paper, we present DVBench, the first end-to-end benchmark for Real-World UVM design verification agents. s5f27fb5aeb.summary: Researchers introduce DVBench, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating agents that perform UVM hardware design verification in realistic workflows.
s5f27fb5aeb.why: Engineers automating chip verification get a workflow-level benchmark rather than isolated subtask tests, which better reflects real verification effort.

sedd00b491e.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation
sedd00b491e.description: arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. sedd00b491e.summary: VisAlloc proposes a dual-level method for on-policy self-distillation in multimodal LLMs, filtering samples and reweighting tokens to focus on visually grounded supervision.
sedd00b491e.why: It offers a training technique for improving visual reasoning in multimodal models by avoiding diluted supervision signals.

sdef63a3cd0.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
sdef63a3cd0.description: arXiv:2611.25071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. sdef63a3cd0.summary: FinVeriQA is an open-source multi-agent prototype for financial question answering over SEC filings and live market data, where Python computes numbers and a model writes cited answers.
sdef63a3cd0.why: It shows an architecture separating routing, computation, retrieval and verification to reduce LLM numeric errors in financial analysis.

s25eee472f0.title: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
s25eee472f0.description: arXiv:2611.25086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Browsers now ship local language models to ordinary endpoints. Google includes Gemini Nano in Chrome to enable productivity features such as summarization, with inference running entirely on the device. These browser-embedded models provide new living-off-the-land opportunities for attackers, each instance a potential post-exploitation engine already installed, signed by the vendor, and invisible to network monitoring. The Gemini model is multimodal, capable of processing files, analyzing screenshots, or conversing with an attacker. s25eee472f0.summary: Researchers show that browser-embedded local language models, such as Gemini Nano in Chrome, can be abused by attackers as post-exploitation engines on endpoints.
s25eee472f0.why: Security teams must consider on-device browser AI as a new attack surface that evades network monitoring and is vendor-signed.

s3dae92b55a.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
s3dae92b55a.description: arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentag
s3dae92b55a.summary: MAWAM is a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates future views and action chunks for coordinated manipulation across multiple robots.
s3dae92b55a.why: It presents a method for coordinating multi-robot manipulation by predicting team actions and their physical outcomes together.

s210c147935.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
s210c147935.description: arXiv:2611.25123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval ind
s210c147935.summary: GrepMem is an index-free, lossless memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents that avoids summarization by retrieving stored context via search.
s210c147935.why: Agent builders facing context window limits get an alternative to lossy summarization that keeps details available for later tasks.

s92aaae3221.title: CRAFT: Constrained Route planning with Adaptive Framework and Template-based code generation
s92aaae3221.description: arXiv:2611.25128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Everyday routing requests are rarely a point-to-point shortest path. A driver may need to visit stops, sometimes in a fixed order, under time budgets or distance limits, and perhaps recharge their EV car along the way. Each combination is a distinct routing problem that classically requires its own algorithm, so no fixed solver covers the space of queries users may ask. This paper presents CRAFT, which takes a constrained routing query as free text and returns a route that satisfies the user's requirements on a real road network. An LLM parses the query and generates four search functions, which a generic graph-search engine executes on the road network. We formalize the underlying problem as State-Expanded RCSP (SE-RCSP), which extends res
s92aaae3221.summary: CRAFT parses free-text constrained routing queries with an LLM and generates template-based code to return routes meeting requirements on real road networks.
s92aaae3221.why: It shows how LLMs can translate varied user routing requests into solver code instead of relying on one fixed algorithm.

sd36c83e667.title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
sd36c83e667.description: arXiv:2611.25167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. We evaluate InflEns on a corpus assembled from seven safety-related benchmarks, which demonstrates that the high
sd36c83e667.summary: InflEns is a mixture of LoRA experts whose training data allocation and inference routing both derive from a location game in a prompt-trait space.
sd36c83e667.why: It proposes making expert specialization inspectable before training and using the same allocation to route at inference.

s72b9e664c6.title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models
s72b9e664c6.description: arXiv:2611.25170v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An observable decision reveals the selected action but does not determine which alternatives were internally represented. Drawing on prospection research and hippocampal forward-sweep observations, we develop Before the Choice, an evidence-oriented framework distinguishing future-directed content, prospective computation, and causal guidance. The framework organizes four experimental contrasts and makes their alternative explanations explicit. Its first test case concerns unchosen trajectories in deterministic symbolic environments. A preregistered low-rank probe evaluated once on a sealed TEST did not meet its criterion (paired accuracy 0.020 versus 0.195 for a text-and-observed-choice baseline; 293 admissible pairs). Exploratory H1b expos
s72b9e664c6.summary: The Before the Choice paper presents an evidential framework for testing whether language models internally represent unchosen alternatives before deciding.

scc8d8ff4bb.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
scc8d8ff4bb.description: arXiv:2611.25191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers
scc8d8ff4bb.summary: A study of 814 RL runs finds that knowledge from an LLM judge used as reward stays largely specific to individual answers and does not transfer to choosing new questions to answer.
scc8d8ff4bb.why: Teams using LLM judges as RL rewards should not assume the judge's knowledge transfers to the trained model's broader behavior.

s1ad85ac116.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
s1ad85ac116.description: arXiv:2611.25194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn
s1ad85ac116.summary: MADJEPA is a medical anomaly detector that uses a multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture trained only on healthy patient images.

s282cfb25ff.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions
s282cfb25ff.description: arXiv:2611.25199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require. We propose VG-Steer, which corrects existing polici
s282cfb25ff.summary: VG-Steer proposes test-time adaptation for frozen robot policies, correcting actions using visual-geometric abstractions aligned in context rather than signals learned from robot datasets.
s282cfb25ff.why: It offers a way to adapt robot policies to out-of-distribution settings with limited real-world data.

s99be32b1b9.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
s99be32b1b9.description: arXiv:2611.25209v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered validation. The ingredients exist across community infrastructure. We outline a staged, measurable path to adoption, intended to reduce silent error.
s99be32b1b9.summary: The paper proposes AWARE, an agent-specific data readiness layer extending FAIR principles for Earth-science data used by autonomous AI agents.
s99be32b1b9.why: Data teams building agents on scientific datasets need requirements beyond FAIR, since agents cannot supply expert judgement.

sa3a7dd4cbd.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
sa3a7dd4cbd.description: arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and produci
sa3a7dd4cbd.summary: ROAM is a system combining a vision-language model with learned locomotion so legged robots can perform kilometer-scale navigation in alpine and urban settings.
sa3a7dd4cbd.why: It demonstrates integrating VLM reasoning with low-level control for long-range robot navigation in unstructured environments.

s7dc0b6c014.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models
s7dc0b6c014.description: arXiv:2611.25226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Provenance schemes such as those based on content watermarks let images from a generative model be traced back to it. A practical watermarking scheme must be accurate at a low false-positive rate (FPR), robust under content-preserving processing, and undetectable. In addition, it must resist forgery; otherwise, even from a single watermarked image and a surrogate model, an adversary can imprint the watermark onto an arbitrary image or regenerate new content that carries it, falsely attributing harmful content to a model or making authentic photographs appear AI-generated. We argue that a watermarking scheme should not only reject forgeries but also report them: a forgery rejected as unwatermarked leaves no trace of the attempt. State-of-the
s7dc0b6c014.summary: The paper presents forgery-evident undetectable watermarks for generative image models, aiming to detect forged watermarks and reject them rather than accept forged attributions.
s7dc0b6c014.why: Provenance systems for generated images must resist forgery, which affects how platforms attribute harmful or authentic content.

s4e21fa0de8.title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
s4e21fa0de8.description: arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy
s4e21fa0de8.summary: Researchers study how user memories stored in LLM parameters should persist or decay, arguing memory systems need lifecycle governance rather than indefinite retention.
s4e21fa0de8.why: Suggests parametric memory designs should include forgetting and updating mechanisms, not just continual learning, to stay deployable.

sed96183733.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation
sed96183733.description: arXiv:2611.25239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable visual perception under degradation requires distinguishing task-relevant content from degradation-induced variations, especially in concealed object segmentation (COS), where foreground cues are inherently weak. The central challenge is not merely improving visibility, but identifying reliable content evidence amid degradation-induced variations. RGB-space segmentation often entangles content and degradation cues, while restoration-based methods primarily focus on image recovery and task interaction. This motivates explicit factorization to distinguish content evidence from degradation effects and assess its reliability. Retinex provides a spatially aligned basis for this separation but remains illumination-centric. We therefore e
sed96183733.summary: Researchers propose explicitly factorizing content from degradation cues to improve concealed object segmentation on real-world degraded images, rather than relying on restoration.

s7989c2a6f0.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
s7989c2a6f0.description: arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these mod
s7989c2a6f0.summary: Researchers present PLANTA, an ontology-based method that jointly adapts robot task plans and architectural configurations during mission planning.
s7989c2a6f0.why: Shows how coupling task planning with architecture reconfiguration may matter for adaptive robotic systems, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s3199791594.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
s3199791594.description: arXiv:2611.25257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. s3199791594.summary: Keel, a agentic weight-editing method, uses a frontier model to find and remove looping behavior in a small vision-language model by rewriting its weights.
s3199791594.why: Offers a new way to repair model failure modes directly in weights instead of only adjusting decoding.

s824e342a43.title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation
s824e342a43.description: arXiv:2611.25258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc rewriting is used to reduce demographic disparities in LLM-generated text when the source model is inaccessible. A rewrite can look successful merely because it improved its own target or satisfied its selector. We study this as a transfer problem on 660 gender pairs and 1,980 age contrasts of demographic-conditioned climate messages. A rewriter proposes edits, a selection model chooses among constraint-satisfying candidates, and an independent evaluator uninvolved in either rates pairwise framing disparity. A fixed policy that always targets the message with the lower Persuasion Bias Index (PBI) transfers inconsistently across axes and outcome aggregations. An adaptive policy that proposes edits on both sides but accepts at most o
s824e342a43.summary: Researchers evaluate post-hoc rewriting to reduce gender and age framing disparities in LLM climate messages, using an independent evaluator to test whether gains transfer.
s824e342a43.why: Shows rewrites can appear successful against their own selectors, so teams need independent evaluators to measure bias mitigation.

sb3e4fb5306.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
sb3e4fb5306.description: arXiv:2611.25288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern recommendation systems face substantial memory pressure, largely from the sparse embedding layer that maps high-cardinality categorical features into dense vectors. In-training embedding pruning (ITEP) removes less important embedding rows during training, yielding end-to-end memory savings but sometimes degrading accuracy because per-table pruning ratios are set by size-based heuristics. We use feature importance (FI) to guide these ratios (FI-ITEP), assigning higher pruning to tables tied to less important features. Across three large-scale recommendation models, FI-ITEP achieves 20--40% total memory reduction while matching or improving accuracy relative to percentile-based ITEP. sb3e4fb5306.summary: Researchers propose guiding in-training embedding pruning with feature importance to set per-table pruning ratios in large recommendation models.
sb3e4fb5306.why: Could reduce memory use in recommendation systems while avoiding the accuracy losses of size-based pruning heuristics.

s8585bfae02.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
s8585bfae02.description: arXiv:2611.25289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than
s8585bfae02.summary: Researchers compare black-box and white-box confidence methods for eleven open-weight LLMs used as zero-shot classifiers across five datasets.
s8585bfae02.why: Gives guidance on which confidence signals to trust when using zero-shot LLMs as classifiers in production.

s4ca1bd2307.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
s4ca1bd2307.description: arXiv:2611.25328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. s4ca1bd2307.summary: ReLay is a bidirectional framework that recovers generator programs from analog layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs.
s4ca1bd2307.why: Could help analog design teams reuse existing layouts and migrate them across process technologies.

s17e39d347f.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
s17e39d347f.description: arXiv:2611.25335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is increasingly applied to scientific imaging domains, such as microscopy, where labels are scarce but noisy data is abundant. These domains exhibit significant signal-dependent noise, which can create a representational shortcut: since both augmented views derive from the same noisy image, the encoder can boost view agreement by also encoding noise patterns rather than semantic content. To enable noise-robust representation learning without knowledge of underlying noise models, we introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation (SEANA), a drop-in module that generates noise-aware SSL views. SEANA learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform (VST) from noisy data, then estimates the clean signal and resamples
s17e39d347f.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation to stop self-supervised learning from encoding noise patterns instead of semantic content in scientific imaging.
s17e39d347f.why: Relevant for teams training self-supervised models on noisy scientific data where labels are scarce.

sb109a6d979.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
sb109a6d979.description: arXiv:2611.25339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. sb109a6d979.summary: Researchers report a verification-gated LLM agent workflow that ported an ML-KEM/ML-DSA post-quantum accelerator to hardware and audited the resulting evidence with mutants and formal checks.
sb109a6d979.why: Shows self-generated tests and reviews from LLM agents can miss flaws, so hardware teams need independent verification.

s667b660cd2.title: FPGA-GEN: Target-Aware RTL Generation via HLS
s667b660cd2.description: arXiv:2611.25351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Successful C/C++ compilation does not guarantee correct or efficient FPGA hardware after high-level synthesis (HLS). FPGA-GEN is an agentic HLS-C generation workflow that encodes specification, readiness, selection, repair, and admission rules in explicit task contracts and bounded tool-feedback loops for candidate-level decisions. On HLS-Eval, five shared-context outputs per task yield 407/425 (95.8%) public-testbench passes. In a cumulative conversion campaign, FPGA-GEN admits 104/107 (97.2%) HLS-LeVeri designs under held-out co-simulation, Vivado synthesis/fit, and same-RTL evidence. s667b660cd2.summary: FPGA-GEN is an agentic workflow that generates target-aware HLS C code, reporting high pass rates on public testbenches and held-out co-simulation.
s667b660cd2.why: Suggests agentic HLS generation with bounded tool feedback can produce FPGA designs that pass rigorous co-simulation.

sb22ec12381.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
sb22ec12381.description: arXiv:2611.25361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods. sb22ec12381.summary: Researchers study task-specific design choices for incorporating argumentation frameworks into LLM decision-making across debate and fact-verification tasks.
sb22ec12381.why: Clarifies that the benefit of argumentation-augmented LLM pipelines depends on how arguments are constructed and evaluated.

s87235c7a31.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
s87235c7a31.description: arXiv:2611.25400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to handle distribution shifts during deployment without source-domain retraining. However, backpropagation-based adaptation incurs heavy memory overhead on resource-constrained robots, whereas zeroth-order (ZO) methods suffer from high estimation variance under limited perturbation budgets. We observe that while ZO estimation enables low-memory adaptation with rapid initial gains, it often stalls or degrades over long-horizon updates due to noisy gradient estimates. To address these limitations, we propose Dune, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations. s87235c7a31.summary: Dune is a zeroth-order optimizer with time-conditioned historical error regression for test-time adaptation of vision-language-action robot models under distribution shift.
s87235c7a31.why: Offers a lower-memory adaptation approach for robots, where backpropagation-based updates are costly on constrained hardware.

s1672a31b55.title: FG-GraphBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multimodal Scene Graphs
s1672a31b55.description: arXiv:2611.25408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-grained visual understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to recognize small visual entities and understand their relationships. Scene graphs offer a natural way to represent this information, organizing visual entities as nodes and their relationships as edges. However, we identify two challenges: existing scene graph benchmarks provide insufficient coverage of fine-grained entities and the relationships among them, and existing methods for fine-grained visual understanding have yet to effectively leverage such graph-structured information in MLLMs. To address these challenges, we introduce Fine-Grained Multimodal Scene Graph Benchmark (FG-GraphBench) and FiGRA. s1672a31b55.summary: Researchers introduce FG-GraphBench, a benchmark with multimodal scene graphs for evaluating and improving fine-grained visual understanding in multimodal LLMs.

s33e27ad16d.title: SGLayout: Schema-Guided Closed-Loop Refinement for LLM-Driven Parameterized Layout Generation
s33e27ad16d.description: arXiv:2611.25410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in parameterized layout generation via tool-augmented code synthesis. However, LLMs lack spatial awareness, making one-shot generation unreliable. While layout quality can be evaluated with established techniques, a critical gap remains: geometric-domain evaluation outcomes cannot be directly translated into actionable code-level fixes, trapping iterative refinement in blind refactoring. We propose SGLayout, a self-refining framework that closes this gap via a schema-guided mechanism. s33e27ad16d.summary: SGLayout is a self-refining framework that uses a schema-guided mechanism to turn geometric evaluation results into actionable code fixes for LLM-generated parameterized layouts.
s33e27ad16d.why: Shows a path to making LLM code-generation refinement loops more targeted than blind regeneration.

sf1c3ab95da.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
sf1c3ab95da.description: arXiv:2611.25412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. This separation makes it difficult to discover previously unknown components whose security relevance becomes apparent only through their potential roles in an exploit chain. We present ChainAgent, a goal-directed LLM-agent framework that jointly discovers exploit-chain components and their capability dependencies in source code. sf1c3ab95da.summary: ChainAgent is presented as an automated system for discovering chainable vulnerabilities in PHP web applications, combining flaw identification with exploit-chain dependencies.
sf1c3ab95da.why: Chained low-severity flaws can enable high-impact attacks, so automated chain discovery could help security teams find risks that isolated scanning misses.

s9d012a181a.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models
s9d012a181a.description: arXiv:2611.25418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) often need to identify small, subtle lesions within high-resolution images containing extensive normal anatomy and redundant visual information. Visual-token compression improves efficiency, but preserving salient regions alone can discard the context needed for diagnostic interpretation. This context can extend across images: in bilateral mammography, the opposite breast provides a patient-specific anatomical reference. Yet retaining such evidence does not ensure that the model uses it effectively. We propose Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning (BESR), which connects evidence preservation with comparative assessment through a bilateral-guided token selector and a bilateral reward. s9d012a181a.summary: Researchers propose a bilateral evidence selection method for mammography vision-language models that uses the opposite breast as a reference for diagnosis.

s3b225ecfb8.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
s3b225ecfb8.description: arXiv:2611.25429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent skills package procedural knowledge as natural-language instructions, and a skill helps only when its instructions are correct and properly followed by the agent. Self-evolving agents revise their own skills from the runs they make, but existing methods judge each run as a whole, by its outcome or by where it went wrong, and cannot tell whether a failure comes from a wrong instruction or from one the agent did not follow. Instruction-level coverage was introduced to test skills and labels each instruction of a run as follow, not-follow, or not covered, which separates these causes. sf9a33d8778.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
sf9a33d8778.description: arXiv:2611.25436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. sf9a33d8778.summary: Raptor is a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to adapt tree-based speculative decoding for vision-language models with long visual contexts.
sf9a33d8778.why: Faster VLM inference with long visual inputs could lower serving costs, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sc2f91161c9.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
sc2f91161c9.description: arXiv:2611.25462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical reinforcement learning enables sequential tasks to be represented as compositions of separately trained skills. This paper evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing their training requirements and task performance with flat reinforcement learning baselines. The evaluation concerns complete pipelines with task-specific observation, reward and control structures. sc2f91161c9.summary: A study evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical reinforcement learning pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation against flat RL baselines.

s7bcc70a701.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
s7bcc70a701.description: arXiv:2611.25469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model.
