s7bcc70a701.summary: DRJanus is a visual camouflage attack that embeds two images in one JPEG, so automated checks see benign SDR content while HDR viewers see harmful content.
s7bcc70a701.why: Content moderation pipelines that read only SDR bases can be bypassed, so teams running image safety checks should account for HDR gain maps.

sca75aaf74d.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
sca75aaf74d.description: arXiv:2611.25471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-based digital twins of air conditioning, a principal energy consumer in manufacturing and buildings, can be generated automatically from a declarative specification of its equipment, connections, and sizing. Large language models (LLMs) now write such specifications from plain-language descriptions. Evaluations of these specifications stop at parse success, completed runs, or textual similarity, and cannot reject a model that converges in simulation but is physically wrong. sca75aaf74d.summary: A four-level executable validation protocol is proposed to test LLM-generated topology specifications for physics-based HVAC digital twins beyond parse success.
sca75aaf74d.why: Simulation convergence alone does not show physical correctness, so engineers using LLM-generated digital twin specs need stronger validation.

se380e40095.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
se380e40095.description: arXiv:2611.25476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. se380e40095.summary: WeightCode uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks via weight-space programming.

s617b4bd409.title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
s617b4bd409.description: arXiv:2611.25477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. We present a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels, a training-only nested-region objective, and a four-expert bottleneck adapter. s617b4bd409.summary: AIstatLab describes a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet for BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3 brain-tumor segmentation, trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels and a four-expert adapter.

s1d9e66af52.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
s1d9e66af52.description: arXiv:2611.25484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each fixed $k$, iterative-width search finds optimal plans in polynomial time on tasks of bounded tuple-chain width, but the approximability of planning width has remained open even when an optimal plan is supplied. When all optimal plans visit the same state sequence, we characterize set and chain width as hitting numbers of competing states. s1d9e66af52.summary: A paper proves that planning width is hard to approximate even when a unique optimal plan is supplied, for positive-precondition STRIPS tasks.

s818f31cc51.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations
s818f31cc51.description: arXiv:2611.25503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech-scene generation aims to synthesize intelligible target speech together with diverse environmental sounds as a coherent acoustic scene. The task is considered challenging in two respects. Speech and environmental audio differ substantially in their semantic and acoustic characteristics, yet existing approaches typically model the complete scene using a single mixed acoustic representation. At the same time, the two sounds are closely related in real-world speech scenes, whereas conventional approaches usually rely on simulated scenes mixed from independently recorded sources. s818f31cc51.summary: Researchers present a joint language modeling approach for speech-scene generation that uses distinct token representations for speech and environmental sounds.

s8c7cb4003b.title: Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Persona's Eyes?
s8c7cb4003b.description: arXiv:2611.25508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models have been used to simulate where a user looks on a web page. However, a persona in the prompt reaches the simulated gaze only partly. We measure this reach as the difference in one model's gaze between two MatrAIx personas that differ in a single attribute. We introduce persona lenses, which place the persona between the model and the page: a text lens (a two-step prompt in which the model first writes what the persona would look at), a pixel lens (marks on the region matching the persona's interests) and a weight lens (a dwell reward gated to keep the scanpath natural). s8c7cb4003b.summary: Persona lenses are introduced to test how much a persona in the prompt affects a vision-language model's simulated gaze on web pages, using text, pixel, and weight lenses.
s8c7cb4003b.why: Measuring how persona prompts shape VLM outputs matters for teams using simulated user attention in UX or ad testing.

s6a41ba8706.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
s6a41ba8706.description: arXiv:2611.25526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. Runtime Guardrail (RG) maps this record to an allow, block, or user-approval decision; Predefined Task Routing (PTR) serves recurring requests through verified routes with post-execution screen checks; and a floating interface keeps execution in a compact overlay. s6a41ba8706.summary: MATE is an execution-layer system that sits between mobile agent action proposals and device effects, using a runtime guardrail to allow, block, or request user approval.
s6a41ba8706.why: Mobile agents touching payments, settings, and private data need enforcement outside the model, and this architecture shows one way to build that boundary.

sc89424b5a2.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
sc89424b5a2.description: arXiv:2611.25527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. We study whole-page optimization, which selects and orders the items on a page jointly to maximize the score of the page. The number of possible pages grows combinatorially, so good pages must be generated rather than enumerated. Some generative re-ranking methods use the same page-level training signal for every choice in a sampled page. Others imitate target pages built before training, which remain largely fixed as the generator improves. sc89424b5a2.summary: Researchers study generative ranking policies for whole-page optimization, selecting and ordering recommendation items jointly to maximize page-level score.

s692dd72e45.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
s692dd72e45.description: arXiv:2611.25529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. s692dd72e45.summary: CoachSI is a robot policy self-improvement method in which a frozen vision-language model coaches the policy in language to supply missing next steps in long-horizon tasks.
s692dd72e45.why: Language-based coaching from a frozen VLM offers a way to improve robot policies without new skill demonstrations, relevant to robotics teams.

s670a117ee6.title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation
s670a117ee6.description: arXiv:2611.25538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently established a new paradigm in machine learning, demonstrating exceptional zero-shot generalization and complex reasoning capabilities. Concurrently, neural network parameter generation has emerged as a promising avenue for rapid task adaptation and model synthesis. Existing weight generation techniques, however, struggle to jointly learn the distribution of diverse models, to encode heterogeneous architectures within a single generator, and to generalize out of distribution. We therefore ask whether pretrained parameters can be encoded into a discrete domain so that the zero-shot generalization LLMs exhibit in text generation can be transferred to weight generation. s670a117ee6.summary: Researchers study autoregressive neural network parameter generation, aiming to learn distributions over diverse architectures and generalize out of distribution.
s670a117ee6.why: Could enable faster task adaptation by generating model weights, but the description only outlines the problem and motivation.

s898898b4ab.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
s898898b4ab.description: arXiv:2611.25557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task-specific rubrics are increasingly used to evaluate open-ended language-model outputs, yet constructing comprehensive evaluation criteria from complex source documents remains challenging. We study automatic rubric construction in professional mergers and acquisitions (M&A) due diligence, where evaluation criteria must be inferred from task instructions and supporting documents without access to an expert-authored reference rubric. We introduce a multi-axis generation framework that explores complementary structural and free-form views of the source evidence to construct a broad pool of candidate evaluation criteria. s898898b4ab.summary: A paper finds that ranking, rather than generation, is the main bottleneck limiting LLM-built evaluation rubrics for M&A due diligence tasks.
s898898b4ab.why: Suggests teams building LLM evaluation rubrics should focus on selecting criteria, not only generating more candidates.

sb7d196b223.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
sb7d196b223.description: arXiv:2611.25567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. sb7d196b223.summary: Researchers propose an online, instruction-conditioned method to detect mistakes in egocentric procedural videos as the video unfolds.
sb7d196b223.why: Relevant to building real-time assistants that flag procedural errors while there is still time to recover.

s38e21e3365.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
s38e21e3365.description: arXiv:2611.25580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. s38e21e3365.summary: FlashX proposes reusing robotic experiences stored in CBA-based NAND flash to warm-start diffusion-based denoising for embodied agents.
s38e21e3365.why: Points to hardware-level storage for experience reuse, which could cut compute for robot policies in unfamiliar environments.

s8e2654b2a1.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
s8e2654b2a1.description: arXiv:2611.25582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. However, developing effective RAG systems requires substantial engineering effort and iterative experimentation, as effective design choices vary across tasks and domains. With rapid advances in LLM agent capabilities, we ask how well these agents can autonomously build RAG systems and how effectively they can improve them through iteration. s8e2654b2a1.summary: AutoRAGBench is introduced as a benchmark measuring how well LLM agents can autonomously build and iteratively improve RAG systems.
s8e2654b2a1.why: Gives engineers a way to measure whether coding agents can handle the iterative engineering work of building RAG pipelines.

s0621fd1c0c.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
s0621fd1c0c.description: arXiv:2611.25584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities. s0621fd1c0c.why: Shows an approach to interpretable multimodal fusion for oncology data, though the description offers limited detail on results.

s94a6a151c1.title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training
s94a6a151c1.description: arXiv:2611.25597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as predictors across various tasks, benefiting from their ability to use information from unstructured context. However, when predictions serve as parameters of downstream optimization problems, higher prediction accuracy does not necessarily translate into lower decision costs. We propose decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL), a framework for post-training LLMs to predict optimization parameters using negative downstream decision regret as reward. s94a6a151c1.summary: Decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL) post-trains LLMs to predict optimization parameters, using downstream decision regret as the reward.
s94a6a151c1.why: Suggests optimizing LLM predictions for downstream decision cost rather than raw accuracy, relevant for LLM-driven planning pipelines.

sfe231af6f5.title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
sfe231af6f5.description: arXiv:2611.25599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly deployed for long-running tasks that execute arbitrary shell commands or programs. sfe231af6f5.summary: Tether is a verified stateful policy engine that monitors system-level actions of autonomous agents, such as shell commands and network calls.
sfe231af6f5.why: Addresses multi-step data flows and side effects that stateless agent guardrails miss, relevant to securing long-running agents.

s4d2782a054.title: On the Informativeness of Structural Stability Bounds for GNNs: GINs versus GATs
s4d2782a054.description: arXiv:2611.25603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stability bounds for graph neural networks limit how much node representations can drift when the graph changes, but they are rarely compared with the simplest alternative: a bound on the distance between any two outputs, whatever the graph. s4d2782a054.summary: The paper derives structural stability bounds for GIN and single-head GATv1 graph networks under non-small edge perturbations and compares them with diameter bounds.
s4d2782a054.why: Clarifies when stability bounds are more informative than simple diameter bounds when choosing GNN architectures.

s8c88c3a53d.title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance
s8c88c3a53d.description: arXiv:2611.25605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-generated bug reports have drawn criticism for unreliable claims and faulty reproducers that burden maintainers. However, as LLM capabilities improve, some maintainers have begun to express more positive views on AI use in bug reporting and maintenance. Understanding this evolution requires examining whether AI-involved reports are becoming more reliable, which uses of AI are associated with valid findings, and how maintainers investigate these reports and act on them. s8c88c3a53d.why: Offers evidence on whether AI-assisted bug reports are improving, useful for maintainers setting triage policies.

s929f905bb6.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators
s929f905bb6.description: arXiv:2611.25617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Splice-Core is a temporal-unary/binary (tub) hybrid general matrix multiplication (GEMM) unit that minimizes low-order accumulation latency, while retaining value-dependent execution for high-order activation bits. s14f97ff01f.title: DAWN: Robust Neural Blind Deconvolution via Alternating Wiener Guidance
s14f97ff01f.description: arXiv:2611.25621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blind image deconvolution (BID) is an ill-posed inverse problem that aims to jointly recover a sharp image and blur kernel from a single degraded observation. Existing training-data-free learning methods for BID, such as those based on the deep image prior (DIP), often utilize external guidance by including model-based estimates as additional loss terms, which underexploits the information these estimates carry especially under nontrivial noise. s14f97ff01f.why: Relevant mainly to imaging researchers; the description gives little on practical adoption or benchmarks.

s66dcfc1fe9.title: AesDistill: Distilling Generative Aesthetics for Image Color Enhancement
s66dcfc1fe9.description: arXiv:2611.25635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Image color enhancement aims to improve visual appeal, but previous methods often learn to reproduce ground-truth expert targets. These targets reflect the preferences of a few experts and cover a limited range of aesthetic choices. Matching them does not ensure stronger aesthetic quality across different tastes and scenes. By contrast, large generative models learn rich visual knowledge from large image collections and often produce vivid, appealing image edits. s66dcfc1fe9.summary: AesDistill distills aesthetic knowledge from large generative models to improve image color enhancement beyond matching single expert targets.
s66dcfc1fe9.why: Shows distilling generative model knowledge into lightweight enhancement tools, though the description lacks result details.

s8dd5d3fc77.title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
s8dd5d3fc77.description: arXiv:2611.25637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated reinforcement learning enables a fleet of robots to jointly learn a shared navigation policy without exchanging raw experience. s4c2ac37cd9.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings
s4c2ac37cd9.description: arXiv:2611.25640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical-image embeddings are increasingly shared in place of raw images for authorized downstream tasks, yet they may reveal sensitive attributes. s9d3ab5da3b.title: DARSY: A Tool for Data-Driven Abstraction and Policy Synthesis for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Dynamics
s9d3ab5da3b.description: arXiv:2611.25654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents DARSY: a software tool for abstraction-based verification and policy synthesis in discrete-time stochastic control systems with unknown dynamics and noise distributions. sb5ff059faf.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
sb5ff059faf.description: arXiv:2611.25656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. sb5ff059faf.summary: Researchers present A$^2$-VLA, a framework where an embodied agent discovers shared tool affordances so a vision-language-action policy can adapt to new tools.
sb5ff059faf.why: It suggests a way to transfer robot manipulation skills to new tool shapes without retraining from scratch, though the text gives few performance details.

s240e91cac0.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
s240e91cac0.description: arXiv:2611.25661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-
s240e91cac0.summary: GRODE-RTL proposes an anchor-centric representation that gives LLMs source-mapped dependency views of RTL code to help repair non-local hardware faults.
s240e91cac0.why: Better context representations could improve LLM-driven hardware bug repair, where root causes and failing outputs are far apart in code.

sed1bbe60cc.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
sed1bbe60cc.description: arXiv:2611.25680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi-stage reasoning. Unlike existing benchmarks that primarily treat visual information as entity recognition and rely on text-based external knowledge, VC-VQA explicitly models the role of visual information by considering both its source (internal vs. external images) and stage of involvement (pre-retrieval vs. post-retrieval). Specifically, VC-VQA requires models to retrieve external visual evidence, identify visual clues before retrieval, and localize, verify, or match retrieved knowledge against the int
sed1bbe60cc.summary: Researchers introduce VC-VQA, a large benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on vision-centric knowledge reasoning and multi-stage visual question answering.
sed1bbe60cc.why: It provides a benchmark that goes beyond entity recognition to test how well multimodal models use visual information in multi-step reasoning.

s7b4a8fa8e2.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
s7b4a8fa8e2.description: arXiv:2611.25683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Although existing vision--tactile--language--action (VTLA) policies incorporate tactile feedback, when and how touch refines actions under changing visual conditions remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{TipDex-VTLA}, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE) compares predicted and measured touch at m
s7b4a8fa8e2.summary: TipDex-VTLA is a vision-tactile-language-action policy that decides when touch should refine actions in dexterous manipulation under changing lighting.
s7b4a8fa8e2.why: It addresses action drift from illumination changes by using tactile feedback selectively, relevant to robotics teams building manipulation policies.

s57d2266077.title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models
s57d2266077.description: arXiv:2611.25703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can associate places with geographic descriptions, but recovering an observed association does not establish an ability to generalize across geographic space. We distinguish geospatial memory, the recovery of location--description associations observed during training, from spatial generalization, the prediction of descriptions for locations in unobserved regions. We investigate whether continuous location representations improve this generalization and encourage geographic knowledge to become spatially organized within an LLM. We frame this organization as a latent spatial field: a learned mapping from locations to descriptions connected through spatial dependencies. Building on a continuous spatial encoder, we
s57d2266077.summary: A study distinguishes geospatial memory from spatial generalization in LLMs and investigates whether continuous location representations improve generalization to unobserved regions.
s57d2266077.why: It clarifies that recalling place-description associations does not imply generalization, a distinction relevant to evaluating LLM geographic capabilities.

s170dc813fa.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
s170dc813fa.description: arXiv:2611.25705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-term memory is essential for personalized agentic systems that interact with users over long time periods, yet current architectures only capture what happened while leaving the reasoning of why it happened to be derived later by underlying LLMs.%, and silo knowledge within individual users. These events can, however, convey not only what a user experienced but also how that experience shaped their behavioral patterns. We introduce STARK, a dual-graph memory architecture which treats these events not just as nodes but also as edges between behavioral insights. STARK maintains an Episodic Graph which records interactions as temporally, causally, and semantically linked episodes; and an Insight Graph which represents LLM-extracted behavi
s170dc813fa.summary: STARK introduces a dual-graph memory architecture for personalized agents that stores events as both nodes and edges to capture why user behaviors occurred.
s170dc813fa.why: It proposes a memory design for long-term personalized agents, aimed at capturing reasons behind user behavior rather than only events.

s31e3aa6b5a.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
s31e3aa6b5a.description: arXiv:2611.25719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict future videos and actions with one backbone, and their imagined future is often seen as a safety signal. We introduce SteerTrace, a targeted universal attack on WAMs that also traces its effect inside the model. One $\ell_\infty$-bounded (4/255) perturbation per model, shared across frames, tasks, and camera views, pushes the executed action toward an attacker-chosen target. On eight WAMs from four families (FastWAM, Faster-WAM, OpenWAM and LingBot-VA) on LIBERO and RoboTwin, it drives task success close to zero and moves the attacked action toward the target. Same-budget noise and BadWAM produce little action shift in the target direction. We use the signed targeted effect to measure how much of the effec
s31e3aa6b5a.summary: SteerTrace presents a targeted universal adversarial attack on world action models that steers executed actions toward attacker-chosen targets and traces its effect inside the model.
s31e3aa6b5a.why: World action models used as safety signals can be steered by a single shared perturbation, a risk for teams deploying robotic policies.

s4ca05d3251.title: Verifying Before Enhancing: Target Evidence Chain Verification for Infrared Small Target Detection
s4ca05d3251.description: arXiv:2611.25724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Infrared small target detection is essential for early warning, surveillance, remote sensing, and space-based target perception. However, infrared small targets are typically tiny, weakly textured, and boundary-blurred, making them difficult to distinguish from complex backgrounds. Moreover, target-like background structures can produce salient responses across multiple scales, making response strength alone insufficient for reliable target discrimination. To address this challenge, we propose VBE-UNet, a Target Evidence Chain Verification Network that assesses candidate reliability beyond response magnitude through complementary evidence cues. Specifically, counterfactual background explanation models local target evidence, while joint evi
s4ca05d3251.summary: VBE-UNet, a network with target evidence chain verification, is proposed to improve infrared small target detection against target-like background structures.
s4ca05d3251.why: It targets detection failures from background clutter in infrared imagery, relevant mainly to surveillance and remote sensing engineers.

s5a91a3357f.title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research
s5a91a3357f.description: arXiv:2611.25732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous factor research requires generating economic hypotheses as well as implementing and testing them. We present Auto-Alpha, a framework that connects report-guided initialization to self-directed research through a test-driven implementation loop. An idea agent proposes economic mechanisms and signal constructions; a research agent develops them with backtest feedback. Semantic audit, quantitative review, and human admission select factors for a persistent library, while an Experience Library retains research insights. Starting from 120 research reports, Auto-Alpha builds an initial library of 32 factors. It then generates new ideas and refines existing candidates, producing 420 implementations and retaining 62 additional factors. W
s5a91a3357f.summary: Auto-Alpha is a framework where idea and research agents autonomously propose, implement, and backtest economic factors, with audit and human admission steps.
s5a91a3357f.why: It shows an agentic pipeline for quantitative factor research with test-driven loops, though the text gives limited results.

s021c11135f.title: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
s021c11135f.description: arXiv:2611.25734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Companion AIs are increasingly used for emotional support, yet distinguishing meaningful engagement from harmful reliance remains difficult. We introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), which operationalizes users' emotional overreliance (EO) as observable conversational behaviors and separately identifies evidence of relational harm (RH), enabling empirical examination of when reliance behaviors co-occur with adverse consequences. Using naturalistic Character.AI and Replika conversations from 110 adults, we found EO-related behaviors in 63.2% of non-roleplay conversations, while observable relational harms appeared in 10.5%. Although EO did not necessarily lead to harm, recurring patterns often co-occurred with harmful outcomes, su
s021c11135f.summary: Researchers introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks to detect emotional overreliance and relational harm in conversations with companion AIs from Character.AI and Replika.
s021c11135f.why: It offers an observable framework for detecting harmful reliance in companion AI products, relevant to teams handling user wellbeing risks.

s4b00c6c137.title: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models
s4b00c6c137.description: arXiv:2611.25735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare language model behaviors can be difficult to study because obtaining them through ordinary sampling can require a very large number of samples. This motivates the behavior posterior sampling problem: given a language model and a behavior of interest, is there an algorithm that efficiently samples from the model's distribution over transcripts that exhibit this behavior? We introduce PosteriorBench, a benchmark for comparing algorithms by their compute cost and by how close their samples are to the true posterior in forward and reverse KL divergence. PosteriorBench contains 21 tasks on Qwen3.5-0.8B with behavior probabilities from $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-1}$, each with exact posterior samples from a corpus of one billion labeled responses. W
s4b00c6c137.summary: PosteriorBench is a benchmark for comparing algorithms that sample rare language model behaviors efficiently, measured by compute cost and KL divergence to the true posterior.
s4b00c6c137.why: It gives a standard way to compare methods for surfacing rare model behaviors without needing huge numbers of samples.

sb7e915c60c.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
sb7e915c60c.description: arXiv:2611.25736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable Radio Access Networks (RANs) enable runtime deployment of traffic-control functions, but selecting the appropriate configuration remains challenging as network conditions and service requirements change over time. Conventional solutions often rely on static rules or learning-based controllers with predefined state and action spaces, limiting their ability to accommodate changing intents. This paper introduces an LLM-driven xApp for traffic control in programmable RANs. The proposed architecture combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding or the processing of incoming E2 measurements
sb7e915c60c.summary: Researchers propose an LLM-driven xApp that selects traffic-control configurations for programmable 5G RANs based on operator-defined service intents.
sb7e915c60c.why: It explores using LLMs to translate changing intents into RAN traffic-control decisions, relevant to telecom network engineers.

sb29d09c480.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
sb29d09c480.description: arXiv:2611.25747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Promptable segmenters answer what a thing is. Dense prediction tasks also ask class-agnostic questions, such as what stands out or hides, how light is blocked, transmitted or reflected, and where structure lies. Robots, surveillance systems and image editors build on their answers. We study promptable concept maps (PCM), which extend SAM 3's promptable concept segmentation from noun instances to maps of concepts named by short noun phrases such as `"transparent object", with "none" as an answer. PCM-Bench groups the standard test sets of seven such tasks by the question they ask. On it, we find that SAM 3 sees more than it detects. Its semantic path responds to many of these concepts, yet a low image-level presence score can block every det
sb29d09c480.summary: The paper proposes promptable concept maps, extending SAM 3 from noun-instance segmentation to class-agnostic concept maps, with a PCM-Bench benchmark.
sb29d09c480.why: It extends promptable segmentation to dense, class-agnostic questions relevant to robotics and imaging systems, though the text gives limited detail.

sb91ac3642b.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
sb91ac3642b.description: arXiv:2611.25760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly carry out long-horizon development tasks, autonomously planning and executing multi-step actions that span files, tools, and sessions. Because developers rarely follow each action, and agents resuming the work depend on records of what was done, the agent's work report often becomes the primary account of what was changed and established. When the report contains false or unsupported claims, it gives recipients false assurance: incomplete work may be accepted without verification, incorrect assumptions about the current state can propagate to later steps and agents, and evaluators that credit stated success may reward the report rather than the work. Yet little is known about what unfaithful reporting looks like i
sb91ac3642b.summary: The paper characterizes and detects unfaithful work reports from coding agents, where reports contain false or unsupported claims about completed changes.
sb91ac3642b.why: Inaccurate agent work reports can lead teams to accept incomplete work unverified, so detection methods matter for agentic development workflows.

sed11311cca.title: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets
sed11311cca.description: arXiv:2611.25763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion language models offer an architectural route to low-budget generation by updating multiple tokens in parallel, which can reduce the number of sequential decoding steps relative to token-by-token autoregressive decoding. However, realizing this advantage at low budgets is challenging, as generation quality often declines when the number of denoising and refinement steps is reduced. Editable diffusion models address this quality loss through post-draft refinement, but useful intermediate results may still be lost before final submission. We introduce CaRR (Commitment-aware Refinement and Recovery), a training-free framework which improves submission quality from a fixed editable checkpoint through updated-context refill and trajecto
sed11311cca.summary: Researchers propose methods to close the quality gap of diffusion language models when decoding under low inference budgets with few denoising steps.
sed11311cca.why: Parallel token updates could cut sequential decoding steps, but quality loss at low step counts limits practical use for latency-sensitive generation.

sd577fb2d90.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
sd577fb2d90.description: arXiv:2611.25788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A collision-free detour can still bring a legged robot to the next stair or ledge a few centimetres or degrees off, and a fixed locomotion skill, factory or learned, can stall or fall. Existing methods prevent this with a robot model or extensive trial and error, but on a new site with unknown skills neither is available, so they cannot be used. We find that a single 27-minute teaching session already supplies what these methods have to derive or learn: for every stair and ledge, one crossing the skill has completed. Our method, passage-conditioned navigation, makes the route remember how each transition was entered, not only where the path went. It stores each taught crossing as an event and, without training or a robot model, enforces it
sd577fb2d90.summary: Researchers present a passage-conditioned navigation method for wheeled-legged robots that uses one 27-minute teaching session to cross stairs and ledges on new sites.
sd577fb2d90.why: It removes the need for a robot model or extensive trial and error when deploying locomotion skills to unknown environments.

sdbaef07fa9.title: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management
sdbaef07fa9.description: arXiv:2611.25840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision-language agents increasingly rely on segmentation tools, and recent work has focused on acquiring the right mask, often treating a good mask as the end point of tool use. But do these agents use the resulting evidence effectively? To answer this question, we need a benchmark that separates evidence use from segmentation quality, spans multiple medical image types, and allows the same mask to be presented in different ways. Existing medical VQA datasets do not jointly provide these properties. We therefore construct Mask-Evidence MedVQA, a 2.5K-example benchmark spanning four image types, where each question is paired with an answer-relevant ground-truth mask and multiple possible renderings. Our study reveals two limitations
sdbaef07fa9.summary: Researchers introduce Mask-Evidence, a benchmark that separates how medical vision-language agents use segmentation evidence from segmentation quality itself.
sdbaef07fa9.why: It tests whether clinical AI agents actually use tool outputs effectively, not just whether they acquire good masks.

s90de285e6f.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
s90de285e6f.description: arXiv:2611.25845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current research agents are moving beyond academic search toward literature synthesis and experiment planning. These workflows increasingly rely on literature retrieval systems, which serve as standalone systems or as components of research agents. However, existing scientific literature retrieval benchmarks mainly evaluate these methods using topical relevance or citation links as supervision, which cannot capture which prior methods are used for empirical comparison. To address this gap, we introduce Lineage, a benchmark for empirical lineage retrieval in AI scientific literature. s90de285e6f.summary: Researchers introduce LINEAGE, a benchmark for retrieving the prior AI papers whose methods are used for empirical comparison, rather than merely topically related work.
s90de285e6f.why: Research agents that plan experiments need retrieval that identifies empirical lineage, which topical relevance and citation benchmarks do not measure.

s90b8968e39.title: On the trajectories of the ID algorithm
s90b8968e39.description: arXiv:2611.25877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ID algorithm decides whether an interventional distribution can be computed from observational data and, when it can, returns a formula in which products, ratios and summations of conditional probabilities are nested inside one another. We study these formulas by following the trajectories of the calls of the algorithm, each of which ends with a tail (an alternation of lines 7 and 2) and an exit, and we derive two main results. First, line~4 and the exit lines fix the single outer summation of the output, while the tail forms everything inside it, both the inner summations and the ratios. s90b8968e39.summary: A paper analyzes the call trajectories of the ID algorithm, which determines whether interventional distributions are computable from observational data, and derives structural results about its output formulas.

sdb9a70323f.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
sdb9a70323f.description: arXiv:2611.25880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than t
sdb9a70323f.summary: Researchers use grammatical evolution over a domain-specific language to search and re-parameterise belief-propagation decoders for quantum error correction codes.
sdb9a70323f.why: Automated search over decoder designs could improve the speed and reliability of error correction needed for practical quantum computing.

s7dcf79bf5a.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
s7dcf79bf5a.description: arXiv:2611.25898v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. Yet a model can reach a fluent, plausible output through invalid reasoning that static benchmarks do not detect, and confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, and spurious demographic shortcuts can pass conventional evaluation. This critical review covers four paradigms in turn: how clinical hallucination arises and why static metrics miss it; the agentic hallucination cascade, in which multi-agent and tool-augmented systems propagate and amplify early reasoning errors; process reward modeling as step-level supervision; and neuro-symbolic grounding, in which formal logic engines, ontology reasoners, and knowledge graphs place verifiable constr
s7dcf79bf5a.summary: A critical review argues that clinical LLMs should be judged on valid reasoning, not just final answers, and examines hallucination in agentic and neuro-symbolic medical systems.
s7dcf79bf5a.why: Correct final answers can hide invalid reasoning, so teams deploying clinical agents need evaluations that check the reasoning chain.

sd6bcf5cd0f.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models
sd6bcf5cd0f.description: arXiv:2611.25916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a constraint puzzle has several correct answers, language models tend to give the same one.We study four open-weight models from three families on symbolic puzzles and multi-solution ZebraLogic variants with exactly known solution sets.Repeated samples concentrate on one default solution far beyond uniform sampling, and different models often share it.Yet models usually produce even rarely sampled solutions when added clues uniquely identify them.On held-out symbolic puzzles, we compare visiting entities in name order with visiting those with the fewest initial candidates first. sd6bcf5cd0f.summary: Study finds language models repeatedly sample one default solution to multi-solution constraint puzzles, and that search order influences which solutions they favor.
sd6bcf5cd0f.why: Models' concentration on default outputs can hide solution diversity, which matters when evaluating or sampling for varied answers.

s2c36f0f7f5.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
s2c36f0f7f5.description: arXiv:2611.25927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. s2c36f0f7f5.summary: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that predicts outcomes of complete action sequences directly, avoiding costly recursive rollouts to speed up planning.
s2c36f0f7f5.why: Lower planning latency at comparable success rates could make latent world model planning more practical for robotics and agents.

sdbae23e464.title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
sdbae23e464.description: arXiv:2611.25955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI platforms are becoming a major gateway to news and current events. This shift risks amplifying existing geographical biases that favour narratives from wealthier countries over those from the Global South. This is particularly relevant in Latin America, which accounts for the largest share of AI usage in the Global South. We examine how information about Latin America changes when users shift from conventional search engines to LLM-based search. We construct a dataset of 1,901 current events across nine Latin American countries, craft realistic queries, and submit them to three search engines and four language models. We vary query language and user location to represent local, diaspora, tourist, and foreign user scenarios. Across 49,207
sdbae23e464.summary: A study finds LLM-based search surfaces less local and less diverse Latin American news than conventional search engines across nine countries.
sdbae23e464.why: Teams building AI search or news features should account for geographic bias that can shift which regional sources users see.

s4fa9b52a1e.title: Energy estimates of open-weight large language models across stated food weights: a dose-response evaluation
s4fa9b52a1e.description: arXiv:2611.25976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We tested whether energy estimates of open-weight large language models (LLMs) scale proportionally with an exactly stated food weight, and whether computing energy density times weight removes the error. Under a prespecified protocol, seven open-weight LLMs estimated the energy of 168 randomly drawn foods from the USDA Food and Nutrient Database for Dietary Studies at nine stated weights, from 0.25 to 4 times the default amount. The primary outcome was the elasticity of the estimate with respect to weight (1: proportional scaling). A two-step estimate multiplied each model's own stated energy density by the weight in code. s4fa9b52a1e.summary: Study tests whether open-weight LLMs estimate food energy proportionally when stated food weight changes, across seven models and 168 USDA foods.
s4fa9b52a1e.why: It shows LLM numerical estimates may not scale correctly with input quantities, a caution for nutrition or quantitative apps.

sfe291d96b4.title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
sfe291d96b4.description: arXiv:2611.25979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Editing a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) capture of a person so that they wear a new garment requires every rendered view to agree on the same garment details. Existing 3D virtual try-on (VTON) pipelines, however, edit training views largely independently and fuse them with hand-designed heuristics such as manually chosen reference views and fixed attention-blending weights. The resulting inconsistencies are baked into the 3D representation and surface as texture drift, blurred prints, and implausible geometry in novel views. We present GS-VTON-MVT, a three-stage framework that combines implicit and explicit 3D reasoning for consistent 3DGS try-on. sfe291d96b4.summary: Researchers present GS-VTON-M, a multi-view transformer with geometry-guided ControlNet for 3D virtual try-on that aims for consistent garment rendering across views.
sfe291d96b4.why: Consistent multi-view editing reduces texture drift and artifacts in 3D Gaussian Splatting avatars, relevant to fashion and graphics pipelines.

sa5e262d625.title: Safe Subgame Resolving in Multiplayer Games
sa5e262d625.description: arXiv:2611.25981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Poker and other games with hidden information are too large to solve in one pass. Strong systems compute a complete blueprint strategy offline and refine it in real time inside the reached subgame. In 2p0s games, a safety theorem guarantees that subgame resolving never increases how much an adversary can gain by exploiting the resolved strategy relative to the blueprint strategy. With three or more players acting independently, no such guarantee exists yet, and heuristic resolving can increase the profile's best-response gap. We prove the first conditional safety theorem for uncorrelated multiplayer subgame resolving, a post-hoc certificate for any delivered update. The best-response gap of the resolved profile exceeds that of the blueprint
sa5e262d625.summary: Researchers prove the first safety guarantee for subgame resolving in multiplayer imperfect-information games with three or more independent players.
sa5e262d625.why: Heuristic subgame resolving can increase exploitability in multiplayer games, so a provable bound informs how game-solving systems are built.

s2284bc3f30.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
s2284bc3f30.description: arXiv:2611.25985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for au
s2284bc3f30.summary: The paper proposes Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), a legal infrastructure concept for governing autonomous AI agents beyond protocol-level and runtime controls.
s2284bc3f30.why: Protocol maturity like MCP and A2A does not supply legal authority for agent actions, which organizations deploying agents must address.

s488c0b46d1.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
s488c0b46d1.description: arXiv:2611.25989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires models to acquire new capabilities while retaining performance on previous tasks. A stability-oriented perspective common in conventional continual learning emphasizes knowledge preservation and interference mitigation. Complementing this perspective, we revisit CRL for vision-language models through policy improvement, a fundamental principle of RL, to preserve acquired performance gains. Using the performance difference lemma, we characterize historical performance changes through the current policy's expected advantages on historical task distributions, motivating replay of historical prompts with the current policy. To allocate limited replay memory, we propose Contrastive Likelihood Repla
s488c0b46d1.summary: Researchers propose policy improvement-guided replay for continual reinforcement learning in vision-language models to preserve gains on earlier tasks.
s488c0b46d1.why: Offers a replay strategy aimed at reducing forgetting when vision-language models learn new tasks sequentially.

se2cb48c5a5.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
se2cb48c5a5.description: arXiv:2611.26018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global Workspace Theory (GWT), a leading theory of consciousness, holds that information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialized processes that use it. Building a workspace into a network does not reveal what the trained network computes with it: a module that reports an answer may have combined a broadcast message with its own knowledge, or merely forwarded an answer computed elsewhere, and task accuracy and ablation cannot tell these apart. We introduce a causal protocol that identifies who computes when modules communicate. se2cb48c5a5.summary: Researchers propose a causal protocol to verify whether a language model's global workspace modules actually compute with broadcast information.
se2cb48c5a5.why: Accuracy and ablation alone can't show which module does the computation, so this offers a more rigorous way to audit modular model internals.

s12b0889e5c.title: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs
s12b0889e5c.description: arXiv:2611.26062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge graphs on the Web are incomplete, and SPARQL answers a query only from the stored triples. Large language models (LLMs) can predict missing facts, but an LLM returns names instead of IRIs and requires one call per binding of a query variable. We present GenSPARQL, a generative extension of SPARQL 1.1 with an operator GENOP that binds values generated by an LLM to query variables during query evaluation. A similarity join maps generated names to entities of the graph, and the query planner invokes the LLM only for the bindings selected by the other graph patterns and filters. s12b0889e5c.summary: GenSPARQL extends SPARQL 1.1 with a GENOP operator that binds LLM-generated values to query variables, invoking the model only for selected bindings.
s12b0889e5c.why: It lets engineers query incomplete knowledge graphs with LLM predictions while limiting costly per-binding model calls.

sae8493cfe4.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
sae8493cfe4.description: arXiv:2611.26073v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. sae8493cfe4.why: It gives teams a statistical basis for deciding when LLM graders can replace human annotation in large-scale labeling pipelines.

sa095af3ff2.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
sa095af3ff2.description: arXiv:2611.26107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretrained vision language model can be directly extended into a unified model with extensive parameter sharing. Specifically, HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both capabilities, while confining task-specific computation to the output side. Yet such a design introduces two key challenges. Generation in pixel
sa095af3ff2.summary: HiUni proposes a unified multimodal model that extends a pretrained vision-language model with extensive parameter sharing between understanding and generation tasks.

sf22d410519.title: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models
sf22d410519.description: arXiv:2611.26117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as generative inference services, where autoregressive decoding makes response length a key determinant of latency and computational cost. This creates an availability risk: adversarial visual inputs can prolong generation and increase serving overhead. Existing energy-latency attacks typically rely on gradients, logits, or token-level feedback, leaving open whether such risks persist when an attacker observes only the final response. We present ChronoPatch, a black-box attack that induces prolonged VLM generation requiring only the final response. sf22d410519.summary: ChronoPatch is a black-box attack that uses adversarial visual inputs to prolong VLM generation and increase serving latency and cost.
sf22d410519.why: It shows an availability risk for hosted VLM services where attackers only observe final responses, relevant to serving cost and capacity planning.

s032491b940.title: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy
s032491b940.description: arXiv:2611.26172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning models often become more accurate when they can generate longer answers at test time. This behavior is known as test-time scaling. However, RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR) usually trains them with a fixed rollout cap. We find that this cap changes model behavior, not only training cost. After training, models use few additional tokens beyond the training budget. They outperform the base models near that budget, but their accuracy stops improving and falls below the base model at larger budgets. The rollout cap thus becomes a learned constraint, that limits model's test-time scaling. We call this effect budget internalization. s032491b940.summary: Fixed-budget RLVR training causes reasoning models to learn to stop near the rollout cap, improving in-budget accuracy but losing test-time scaling gains.
s032491b940.why: Rollout caps used in RL training can silently change model behavior, so teams should check accuracy across budgets, not only at the training cap.

s1851f0ab4d.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
s1851f0ab4d.description: arXiv:2611.26179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we firs
s1851f0ab4d.summary: RegionAgent uses two-stage preference optimization to apply different restoration actions to different degraded regions of an image.

s209f641b03.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
s209f641b03.description: arXiv:2611.26221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programs increasingly call large language models (LLMs), filling prompt placeholders with program values and consuming the output. Such a call crosses the boundary between natural language and programming language (NL/PL). To follow data across it, an analysis needs a data-flow summary of which placeholders the output uses, but no code describes what the model does. Analyses of these LLM-integrated applications therefore taint every output with every input, creating spurious flows, or ask a second model to label each call, which is costly. s209f641b03.summary: Sightline proposes calibrated data-flow summaries for LLM calls so static analysis can track which prompt inputs affect outputs without spurious flows.
s209f641b03.why: Tainting every output with every input creates false flows; calibrated summaries could make security analysis of LLM-integrated apps more precise.

sba5b1385d3.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
sba5b1385d3.description: arXiv:2611.26242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. sba5b1385d3.summary: FastRoverVLA decouples visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution, reusing plans between expensive inference calls for off-road autonomous driving.
sba5b1385d3.why: Reusing predictions with motion-aligned action buffers reduces costly multimodal inference in robotics control loops.

sd5e23cda01.title: STAGE: Spatio-Temporal Augmented Graph Expansion for Weakly Supervised Cross-Tweet Event Causality Discovery
sd5e23cda01.description: arXiv:2611.26255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Causal relations in disaster-related social media of- ten span independent posts, making cross-tweet causal discovery difficult to supervise and model at scale. We propose STAGE, a framework that separates scalable cross-tweet weak-supervision construction from spatio-temporal relational learning over event occurrences. Starting from local causal seeds, STAGE retrieves semantically related event occurrences across tweets and uses a causal scorer to construct weakly labeled cross-tweet pairs. These pairs supervise a multi-head Graph Attention Network over semantically enriched event representations and a spatio- temporal context graph. We evaluate STAGE on California Wildfire and Hurricane Harvey using human-gold cross-tweet test sets and 15
sd5e23cda01.summary: STAGE is a weakly supervised framework that discovers causal relations across disaster-related tweets using spatio-temporal graph attention networks.

s60c46cfb99.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
s60c46cfb99.description: arXiv:2611.26256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly reuse executable capabilities through skills, but a skill that works on one OS may fail on another because OS assumptions are spread across guide text, scripts, metadata, install contracts, and local entrypoints. Diagnosing such failures by running every skill on every OS is expensive: many executions spend model tokens, runner time, and review effort before revealing whether the failure is truly OS-related. We present SkillBridge, a contract-based workflow with three stages: static analysis, dynamic validation, and repair. s60c46cfb99.summary: SkillBridge is a contract-based workflow that statically analyzes, dynamically validates, and repairs cross-OS compatibility defects in LLM agent skills.
s60c46cfb99.why: Agent skills that break across operating systems are costly to diagnose by brute force, and this offers a cheaper triage and repair approach.

sfcaa8d7359.title: Digitization of Analogue Gauges using Computer Vision
sfcaa8d7359.description: arXiv:2611.26262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Analogue gauges remain prevalent in manufacturing industries for measuring physical quantities, yet manual monitoring by operators introduces human error and operational inefficiency. This research developed and evaluated an automated gauge reading system using computer vision and deep learning techniques. Three hybrid approaches were implemented and compared: OpenCV with Scikit-Image (traditional computer vision), OpenCV with ResNet18, and OpenCV with VGG19 (deep learning approaches). A comprehensive dataset of 1,848 pressure gauge images (0-10 BAR range) was curated through web scraping, synthetic generation, and augmentation techniques. The experimental results demonstrate that ResNet18 significantly outperforms the alternatives, achievi
sfcaa8d7359.summary: Researchers compared three hybrid computer vision approaches for automatically reading analogue pressure gauges using a dataset of 1,848 images.

s16dbbb5159.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
s16dbbb5159.description: arXiv:2611.26282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning capabilities in large language models have evolved from prompting-based methods to internalized model behaviors. In this paper, we investigate whether the internal thinking model of an LLM can be deliberately changed and whether such a change is beneficial. Instead of relying on Chain-of-Thought, we train models to follow Question--Option--Criteria (QOC), a structured decision process that decomposes a task into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria. We present a three-generation development pipeline that ranges from a basic QOC decision core to richer answer synthesis and statistically enriched QOC reasoning. s16dbbb5159.summary: Researchers train LLMs to follow a Question-Option-Criteria decision process instead of Chain-of-Thought, testing whether changing internal thinking helps.

s23b4d8aebf.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
s23b4d8aebf.description: arXiv:2611.26286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS journals. A third ICLR review of a paper added 5.46 new problems to the other two in 2027, against 6.12 in 2026. We apply MELD, a detector of LLM-generated text, to all reviews. Within a paper, two reviews that MELD flags overlap more than two unflagged reviews: by 3.0 points at ICLR in 2024-2025, by 4.5 points in 2026-2027, and by 5.4 points across five journal sources. s23b4d8aebf.summary: A study finds critique overlap in ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML and journal peer reviews rose year-on-year, with LLM-flagged reviews overlapping more within papers.
s23b4d8aebf.why: Growing LLM-generated reviews homogenize feedback, which matters for teams relying on peer review or automated review signals.

sa75cb483e6.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
sa75cb483e6.description: arXiv:2611.26300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Photonic GHZ states generated with probabilistic pair sources can be described by edge-coloured, complex-weighted graphs. In this representation, conditioning on an event with one photon in every detector turns the output amplitudes into coherent sums over perfect matchings, and generating an \(N\)-photon \(D\)-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing a monochromatic quantum graph. sa75cb483e6.summary: Researchers prove a no-go theorem: no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for even N≥4 when D≥N, with the proof found using AlphaProof Nexus.

s63b3db4c8d.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
s63b3db4c8d.description: arXiv:2611.26316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. However, most pathology foundation models are trained on tissue patches and capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either restricted to specific cell populations or rely on computationally expensive architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters. s63b3db4c8d.summary: Researchers present C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model for learning features of individual cells in histopathology images.
s63b3db4c8d.why: Offers a smaller cell-level pathology model as an alternative to large architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters.

s32350dbf39.title: A Control-Theoretic Approximation to Predictive Coding Dynamics
s32350dbf39.description: arXiv:2611.26319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Backpropagation remains the dominant method for training deep neural networks, but its reliance on non-local computations has motivated the search for biologically plausible alternatives. Two prominent frameworks, predictive coding (PC) and deep feedback control (DFC), offer distinct approaches to local learning, yet their relationship remains unclear. Here, we show that DFC arises as a local approximation to predictive coding dynamics near fixed points, with exact equivalence in shallow linear networks and systematic deviations arising with depth, nonlinearity, and distance from equilibrium. s32350dbf39.summary: A paper shows that deep feedback control arises as a local approximation to predictive coding dynamics near fixed points.
s32350dbf39.why: Clarifies the relationship between two biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation, which may inform local learning methods.

se12a03b4bc.title: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers
se12a03b4bc.description: arXiv:2611.26334v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video diffusion transformers reuse key--value (KV) caches across denoising steps, which quickly becomes a bottleneck for long video generation. se12a03b4bc.summary: Researchers propose Temporal Rotation Quantization, a method that rotates adjacent video-frame KV-cache vectors to enable 2-bit quantization in video diffusion transformers.
se12a03b4bc.why: Targets the KV-cache memory bottleneck that limits long video generation, which matters for inference cost and serving.

s3f5bd3f18f.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
s3f5bd3f18f.description: arXiv:2611.26336v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale. Alikbachan is a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified along three crossed axes: a human-validated cultural-distance band, six task types, and a five-family, 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. s3f5bd3f18f.summary: Researchers introduce Alikbachan, a stratified Bengali benchmark for detecting LLM hallucinations across task types and failure modes.
s3f5bd3f18f.why: Provides a consolidated evaluation resource for hallucination detection in a low-resource language.

s03c4c81c2c.title: Beam Model Technical Report
s03c4c81c2c.description: arXiv:2611.26358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. Pretrained on 23.8T diverse, curated, high-quality tokens, Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase, built on verifiable, correctness-anchored data. s03c4c81c2c.summary: Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters, is described in a technical report.
s03c4c81c2c.why: Reports a large open-scale MoE model claimed to need 3-4x less inference compute than comparable models, relevant to deployment costs.

s8a47b51d52.title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
s8a47b51d52.description: arXiv:2611.26398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. Documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) are reconstructed into hierarchical section trees and indexed with structured metadata. s8a47b51d52.summary: Researchers describe an agentic AI ecosystem that consolidates EU-funded water governance project documents into a knowledge base with agentic RAG access.
s8a47b51d52.why: Shows a concrete pattern for applying agentic retrieval-augmented generation to scattered organizational document collections.

s1df0259655.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
s1df0259655.description: arXiv:2611.26407v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. se25f9a5324.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
se25f9a5324.description: arXiv:2611.26420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. se25f9a5324.why: A large synchronized whole-body human motion dataset could help train loco-manipulation policies for humanoid robots.

sb6ebc22a15.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware
sb6ebc22a15.description: arXiv:2611.26437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier text-to-image (T2I) foundation models predominantly rely on multi-billion parameter Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) pretrained across massive compute clusters, creating an accessibility barrier for academic laboratories. When training DiTs from scratch on single consumer GPUs (e.g., an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24\,GB VRAM), practitioners encounter three primary bottlenecks: quadratic attention sequence costs, Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation graph breaks induced by variable aspect-ratio bucketing, and an autoencoder throughput wall where frozen Variational Autoencoder (VAE) operations dominate step latency. s5ac8cfe6f5.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
s5ac8cfe6f5.description: arXiv:2611.26444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback.
